All of what's going for this game is ruined by one single thing. The cube mini game.
So you know what Minecraft is right? Cute little game where you walk around pick up and place cube for creativitys sake that's all good right RIGHT? Hahaha well imagine if that whole system was fit inside of a point and click adventure game to advance MOST of the progression where it does not FIT at all.
In this mini game you collect certain color cubes and throw them into this giant windy pillar elavator thing, once you throw in a sufficient amount you win the game. Seems simple enough right? I do that everyday irl of course. Only if you fall into the water at the bottom you lose the cubes you threw in. There's an enemy that constantly destroys cubes you try to pick up and if they FALL into the water they're gone for good. OH BUT OH HOHOHO, I ALMOST FORGOT sometimes the pillar will just disable and not work. There's great situations like using the elavator to get to a higher floor only to turn off on you sending you straight to the water losing all of your cubes. AND not to forget that you could be throwing cube at it and it just disables with no warning. It doesn't help that the animation is so ambigious if its on or off or not. It's the most frustrating experience even when you know about the platform trick. Because you realize the cubes don't respawn in the play area, you have to either duplicate ones in an awkward way or travel through different floors or jump to other blocks. If you run out of cubes to throw in, you might as well restart. I've actually gotten pretty good at this mini game and still hate it. When I hear the completion ding of the mini-game I can only feel my face sinking into both my hands.
Looking at the screenshots you can probably imagine what you're in for, an interesting first person adventure game with some cool visuals and big open field. Only, one screenshot really stands out, that cube world area screenshot. Look at this screenshot. LOOK AT IT and realize this is what the game is going to put you through several times to advance the story. This whole thing really puts forth the common design issue of: IF THE PLAYER DIDN'T SIGN UP FOR IT,
FORCE THEM TO DO SOMETHING THEY DIDN'T SIGN UP FOR. While the mini-game is somewhat tied to the lore (which is hilarious since in context it's apparently tied to therapy, THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THERAPY) but sometimes you're better off just going out into the backyard and shooting the damn dog. Get rid of the mini-game and find something that fits with the rest of the game would be my suggestion. You could argue it creates variety, but punching myself in the face occasionally would give anything variety. Admittingly, it really seems like they ran out of ideas for the rest of the point and click puzzles. But making an unfitting mini game isn't going to make up for that.
Speaking of which, the point and click puzzle sections are serviceable although the beggining section manages to make cooking a stew the most hardest thing in the world. Knowing how combining items work and the inventory and such was really awkward. But once it gets going it's alright... until the cube game sections.
The only thing this games got going for is its production values and attention to the visual details. I feel like when it comes to the overall story: the ending wasn't worth the trouble. The characters are hard to care for and there's just no emotion to any of their motives. The backstory to the world and why you're here is interesting especially since it takes place in a valley in Mongolia. The shrine in particular reminds me of what my buddhist family tends to have, props to the people who did the...props. If you're looking for a somewhat interesting scifi concept story then this isn't the worst way to spend your time, it's only 5 hours and just don't be afraid to look up a guide to phase through the annoying parts. There was one flower puzzle where I'm sure the yellow ones are completely bugged. If you're still not detterred by all of this then get it on sale if you must.

Baldur’s Gate 2 is a towering achievement in the history of role-playing games. Since 2000, when Black Isle Studios finally released this role-playing game (rpg) sequel of its signature series Baldur’s Gate, the fan community has significantly grown in numbers.
This lavishly produced game quickly established itself as the most compelling, intelligent and exciting rpg available for PC. After Fallout, Planescape: Torment and Icewind Dale it was the next milestone of unparalleled quality, its renown extending far beyond the boundaries of the genre.
The protagonist and companions have an incredible chemistry, and are surrounded by some of the most vivid and compelling fantasy creatures ever created. The storytelling is epic, and the memorable characters offer loads of witty and mature dialogues. Furthermore, the different classes, alignments and team combinations create an amazing replayability.
During the game's development, a quality assurance department was added to BioWare, and the game's publishers lent their assistance in testing. Because of its immense size with over 300 quests, Baldur's Gate 2 was considered a tester's nightmare.
Estimated time for 100 % completion: +200 hours
Singleplayer achievements: 93
Multiplayer achievements: none

No words in any language on Earth can adequately describe the greatness that is the Baldur's Gate series.
This game is a shining example of what a roleplaying game truly is. A lot of it comes from the fact It is based on 2nd Edition Dungeons & Dragons, and while that edition is particularly confusing to learn, it comes to you pretty fast. Most of the learning curve comes from spells and their interactions, and some unintuitive things like "lower is better" for Armor Class, THAC0, and attack speed.
The story is one of the best ever written for an RPG, and it is beautifully voiced to boot! The artwork and graphics, while technically dated, hold up incredibly well in this day and age. They give the game a fantastic sense of character that immerses you into the world with ease. Characters in the game are very fleshed out and are full of dialogue that makes the game world feel like a living, breathing place. This is one of the few RPG's where you can actually roleplay. (GASP! , SHOCK!) In fact, the game is practically designed around you roleplaying your character the way that YOU want. For example, it doesn't punish you for playing one alignment or the other, nor does it accomodate playing one alignment over the other. Characters simply react to you appropriately to your alignment vs, their own.
To anyone who has played the game before the EE came out, the game is now better than ever.
Some very good improvements I've noticed:
- Updated UI, much more functional and friendly
- Graphics as a whole feel more polished
- Revamped spell effects look AWESOME!!
- New recruitable party NPC's fit into the world seamlessly, and have very fun side-quests to boot
- Brand new areas to explore with fun rewards for doing so
(These are only some of the many improvements to the game, there are too many good ones to list here.)
This game is an absolute masterpiece. Anyone who enjoys RPG's will fall in love with this game and its previous game (Baldur's Gate) instantly. It is worth every fraction of a cent and more. Ultimately this game deserves your time and you should buy it immediately ;)

American Truck Simulator consists of delivering cargo to different places in America. Currently, there are 3 states in the game: California, Nevada and Arizona, and I believe that there will be more added in the future. For now though, 3 states is still plenty, as it still takes a great deal of time to travel from one end to the other. In the game, you must follow traffic rules, and drive like a normal human being, though if you wish you can disable traffic offenses and fatigue in the menu. There are around 20 different companies to perform jobs for in these states in this map. There are even some secret areas that aren't displayed on the map. There are lots of things to do in the game, but just incase you get bored, there is the Steam Workshop and TruckersMP, where you can truck along with other players.
Currently, there are not many trucks in the game, at least compared to ETS2, as there are only two truck companies which are Peterbilt and Kenworth. There are also only a few different trucks, though this is likely to change throughout updates. Trucks are fully customizable, though, so you can easily edit the looks and performance of your truck as you go. The trucks handle like a real truck would. They are heavy, making them less controlable, and are slow, especially with trailers.
Most things in the game are unlocked via levelling up, like trucks and truck parts. As you level up, you can also select a perk such as longer distance jobs, or fragile deliveries, as these give you extra money.
As you progress in the game, you can unlock and upgrade garages which allow you to hire workers if you already have a truck for them. These workers can perform jobs for you, earning you even more money.
The game looks pretty good, and has some realism to it. Textures are good looking, and so are the models for buildings and cars. My only issues are that on the highest setting, you can see parts of the map rendering and doing the opposite, amd that cities are just a few buildings. Once you have seen one, you have seen most of them. Some cities have houses in the distance, though you cannot drive near these.
The audio fits the game pretty well. The vehicle sounds are spot on, as far as I can tell. The music is calm, and fits the game very well. The player can also use the radio, which allows you to listen to real radios while you drive, if they so wish.
In my opinion, ATS is a fun game to pass time. There is lots to do in the game, and even more to do with the Workshop and TruckerMP. The graphics are good, the gameplay is great, and so is the audio. If you are thinking about this game, I would recommend Euro Truck Simulator 2 first, as it is similar though more complete.

Zombie Vikings is a side-scrolling beat 'em up which you can play solo or with friends (total 4 players).
The game features about 30 levels which is impressive.
Plot is nothing that would keep you interested. It goes: So one day Loki came and took Odin’s one good working eye. Then Odin raises four misfit Vikings from the dead to retrieve his eye.
Basically you beat up a ton of bad guys going through the levels. Before each level you choose from one of the four Vikings at the start to play level.
Each one has a various amount of different movies to try. While moving left to right in the 2D backdrops, players come across plenty of bad guys to pummel, coins to collects, and side quests to partake in.
Yes, there are side quests in each level that can be found and completed for a new weapon.
Each one has a small little story event and some range, from rescuing a duck from the clutches of an evil fish, to trying to throw pepper into a whales face to make him sneeze the wandering child out of his blow hole.
The majority of gameplay will be this combat over and over again. The side quests do help add variation though, and sometimes there are unique situations where players have to run for their life from an approaching mob, or dodge exploding fish turds.
Also the few boss battles are fun and require a different strategy then the normal battles.
Various weapons can be unlocked or purchased with gold, all perform similarly, yet some have various different effects.
One weapon might give some health back, another electrocutes the enemies, and one features a cat on a stick that scratches enemies.
Runes can also be purchased, some that allow specific characters to increase their abilities or ones that can apply to all playable characters.
The humor won’t be for everyone, but if players can appreciate absurd, crude, and zaniness, this will be one they can appreciate.
All in all it is good game. Nothing special but has it moments.

Bardbarian is a nice tower style RPG action defense type of game (if that is even a thing?!)
In Bardbarian you play as Brad who set's out to defend the precious towns Crystal (and protecting all the residents of the town) calling upon the help of various useful warriors, ninja's, medics etc that are all available for you to choose your own army.
The core mechanic of the game is basically a scrolling from left to right action fest where anything that moves or comes your way from the right you must use your own chosen small army to ensure they are taken out before they come anywhere near the town's crystal and inflict damage.
Bardbarian is a large game that has tonnes of replayability and XP grinding (that doesn't seem much of chore). It has a nice mechanic that keeps the game flowing along nicely allowing you to upgrade your arsenal of chosen Warriors after each fight is over!
Being an Indie game it is sometimes hit and miss with what graphics can be on offer but I personally found the overall 'sheen' and 'quality' to be of a very high standard.
The music seems to suit the game well, I liked the touch of the little guitar 'licks' each time you engaged Brad to summon a warrior or power. I accidently left the title screen music playing for about 30 mins on once occasion and it didn't grate on me either which is definitely not a bad thing.
Pros
+ Pleasing high-quality graphics and production.
+ A Casual game but still has that 'one more game before I turn it off.. appeal!'.
+ Wide arrays of characters for your arsenal of good guys.
+ Extra game modes to play alongside the main campaign.
Cons
- Took a long time to figure out the correct (and best) upgrade paths for your team.
- Can have a frustrating one hit death to your main character Brad at the most inconvenient times.
Bardbarian is a high-quality Indie title that I personally enjoyed playing through, yes it can be frustrating at times but as soon as you have put some time and effort into the game it will reward you with revisiting the same levels but the game being a lot easier to conquer (having a team with fully upgraded warriors!).
Recommended purchase if on sale or part of a bundle!

A nice little platformery romp that's neither too hard nor too easy. Or especially original, but it does what it does well enough that I can forgive that.
Something like half the game or so is a super meat boy-esque platforming engine, with wall jumps and decently fast move speed and all that. Unfortunately, the physics here have a few issues; walljumps will randomly fail to activate, and air control is next to non-existent. Clearing the main game and all the challenge levels did not help me understand how momentum in the air works in the slightest; fortunately air control isn't a big factor in the game. The level design here is pretty solid throughout, throwing in a variety of standard platforming elements; crumbling floors/walls, gravity switches, precarious jumping puzzles, all the usual. Again, nothing new, but done well enough that it works. The last string of levels in the main game and about half the challenge levels fall victim to some platforming sins, unfortunately, but aside from them there's a lot to like here.
Another quarter of the game is basically VVVVVV-lite; you play as a young girl who can't jump but can switch between floor and ceiling. The main issue here is that she has literally no weight to her at all and very casually floats up and down with gravity switches; it really feels awkward and not especially well-executed. Fortunately the levels here never get too difficult and this mechanic seems to be axed earlier than the others for some reason. There are some interesting puzzles, but this section also tends to have the issue of the background hiding collectibles.
The last quarter is a runner-style game incorporating more gravity-switching; often accompanied with rather precise jumps and well-placed enemies. The tail-end of these levels also fall victim to long sequences of really tight jumps, and a wind mechanic introduced near the end leads to sudden physics changes that are barely visible on-screen. Other than that these levels are competent enough.
Tying the whole thing together is visuals that remind me most specifically of Knytt Underground and LIMBO; black foreground and characters of the latter and vibrant backgrounds behind dark foreground of the former. The music is a very relaxed soundtrack that helps lessen frustration and is really quite pretty; not that special but it serves its purpose well.
Also there might be a story here, but not really, it's mostly platforming action.
The main game will run you about 3 hours, maybe more if you go for all collectibles/time trials/no death runs. It's not especially long but it's not especially expensive either and I certainly don't regret buying it.

There is also a rather large mod scene that I would suggest folks look into (after the first playthrough, of course).

With it, I – and anyone else with enough time and patience – can  jump straight into the development of an RPG. Don’t be fooled, however; to make something presentable is a daunting task that requires proficiencies in several disciplines.

The toolset is clean and impressive; with dozens of hours clocked I have not experienced a bug yet. The engine is well supported by staff answering questions on the forums and updates every few days, either with new assets, bugfixes, or rolling out a new editor. Getting a handle on the controls is no more difficult than taking an hour to watch a tutorial or two, then playing with it yourself on a demo map.
Also, if EARLY ACCESS isn’t enough of a hint to you, it’s not complete. What is there is fully functional and fantastic and the rest is quickly on the way, but do NOT be like the other people on here and feign surprise when they were perfectly aware they were purchasing an incomplete product.

I was quite impressed when I first saw this, although it is in early access the software has a top notch terrian/world editor with a simple and intutive interface. It also has quite a lot of free assets that are reasonable quality. I also like the direction the devs have talked about, they seem to be shooting for a similar set up to rpgmaker in terms of how various editors will work to set up game logic and so forth.
However, I later found out that the world editor is 3D Torque (an already released game engine). In other words at the moment this is a stripped down version of 3D Torque (which is free) plus some models. Unfortunately that has severely dented my confidence in the future of this project, since the impressive world editor (which is the only thing that is working) was actually made by someone else.
Now the Torque 3D is engine is available under the MIT license so there is nothing illegal about it, but I find it almost unbelievable that the devs have slapped their label/splash screen onto the Torque 3d world editor added a few assets and started selling this as their own work in early access without having finished any of their own "editors" for  it.
I do hope the devs actually finish the vision they have for the software, but at this point I can't recommend buying software that you can basically download for free from GarageGames. And I can't help but feel somewhat outraged that they are basically selling someone elses work, without even giving credit to programmers that made it.

Submerged is a brief game that tells a simple story using good art direction, soundtrack, and gameplay mechanics.
Pros:
- Simple control scheme is easy to use
- Relaxing music
- Graphics are nice to look at even if they aren't AAA quality
Cons:
- The controls feel a little too simple at times, with the lack of a jump or run button.
- At $20, it's vastly overpriced for what you get
- 2 hour playtime if you don't attempt to find any of the extras
- Due to the open world nature of the game, all the "levels" are basically the same difficulty.
- There's no system of levelling up or gaining new abilities, so a single playthrough is very straightforward.
Either/Or:
- There is no combat system, nor is there a sense of health or damage in the game. Your boat can knock into buildings and fish without taking damage and there's no way for Miku to lose health (as it's not even a mechanic in the game). This can make it more enjoyable for people who are in it for the puzzle aspect alone, or frustrating for people who want more of a challenge.

Tengami is an adventure game done up like a pop-up book. You click around to guide a little paper samurai through idyllic Japanese landscapes in his search for cherry blossoms. There are puzzles where you have to pull tabs or fold parts of the pages to make new paths or reveal new landmarks, and the transitions between areas are done by turning the pages. A few of the puzzles are pretty clever, and the landscapes are really quite pretty.
That's about the extent of the nice things I can say about the game. First and foremost, there's very little gameplay. There are three chapters, and each chapter is roughly broken up into a nature part and a building part. The nature part is mostly you walking around landscapes and solving simple puzzles to open paths. These are nice and relaxing, but your paper samurai walk slow enough to get annoying by the second chapter or so. The building part is when you arrive at a shrine or pagoda and do more intensive puzzling, usually by finding an item and solving combination locks and such. These start easy, get interesting, and then fly past that into annoying by the end.
Even if you like the gameplay, you get less than an hour of it. The three chapters are seriously about 15-20 minutes long. Considering most of that is watching your dude walk around, that's appallingly short. The art can't carry it either, really... while the origami landscapes are pretty at first, there's very little detail and a severe lack of interaction. The empty, static feeling to them makes the charm wear off fast. In addition, the pleasant music cuts out at strange times, and the loading times are inexplicably long. And don't play it for the story, either, because there isn't one. At all. Your dude wants to find cherry blossoms to make his tree bloom. He finds them, it blooms, the end. Honestly you won't get anything more out of this game than you did by looking at the screenshots.

Beautiful game, I can definitely see why it was included in the Eye Candy Humble Bundle. The visuals are lovely, and the concept of a pop-up book is awesome and well executed. That being said, the game is short and the puzzles not particularly challenging - playthrough lasts maybe 90 minutes if you take your time observing everything and watch the credits. Good for a casual, atmostpheric play without stress, but I could have wished for a bit more meat to it. I also wish there was a challenge mode where they leave off all the little cues showing what can be moved or flipped. In all but one case I noticed, there were subtle visual cues that something could move (texture and color changes, edges not quite lining up) and hunting for these would add a challenge and extend play time.
Many people complained about how slow he moves, but it felt about right for a point-and-click with this kind of atmosphere; cultivating patience when retracing steps has always been a necessity in point-and-click, and the transition animations between pages are nicely quick. The only complaint I had was how long it took to load the next area (and that's nothing new, either).
If you like to support indie games with novel ideas and the art put into them, it may be worth the $10 to you; for most, I suspect it won't be worth that much. But at 75% off, it would be worth picking up to play through if it looks at all your speed.

No words in any language on Earth can adequately describe the greatness that is the Baldur's Gate series.
This game is a shining example of what a roleplaying game truly is. A lot of it comes from the fact It is based on 2nd Edition Dungeons & Dragons, and while that edition is particularly confusing to learn, it comes to you pretty fast. Most of the learning curve comes from spells and their interactions, and some unintuitive things like "lower is better" for Armor Class, THAC0, and attack speed.
The story is one of the best ever written for an RPG, and it is beautifully voiced to boot! The artwork and graphics, while technically dated, hold up incredibly well in this day and age. They give the game a fantastic sense of character that immerses you into the world with ease. Characters in the game are very fleshed out and are full of dialogue that makes the game world feel like a living, breathing place. This is one of the few RPG's where you can actually roleplay. (GASP! , SHOCK!) In fact, the game is practically designed around you roleplaying your character the way that YOU want. For example, it doesn't punish you for playing one alignment or the other, nor does it accomodate playing one alignment over the other. Characters simply react to you appropriately to your alignment vs, their own.
To anyone who has played the game before the EE came out, the game is now better than ever.
Some very good improvements I've noticed:
- Updated UI, much more functional and friendly
- Graphics as a whole feel more polished
- Revamped spell effects look AWESOME!!
- New recruitable party NPC's fit into the world seamlessly, and have very fun side-quests to boot
- Brand new areas to explore with fun rewards for doing so
(These are only some of the many improvements to the game, there are too many good ones to list here.)
This game is an absolute masterpiece. Anyone who enjoys RPG's will fall in love with this game and its previous game (Baldur's Gate) instantly. It is worth every fraction of a cent and more. Ultimately this game deserves your time and you should buy it immediately ;)

For my taste this game is too evil, to put it simply. There's no room for being morally "good" in a real or fantasy sense of the word. Kidnapping, murder, torture, human sacrafice and cannibalism are not just present, they are central components of the game. A big part of the game is capturing people who are then tortured into submission and used as slaves. You can play and enjoy the game while not engaging in this, but it leaves you crippled and ultimately you can't even use most of the content. In short, you have to enjoy playing as an evil, demented sick freak in order to really get into this game. Of course someone can try to paint it a little prettier than that, but imo this is what the game is. Add to that the absurd gore (you hit someone with a sword and they suddenly collapse into a pile of dismembered body parts and blood) and the whole thing is... well it's just not for me, and it's a little disturbing how many people seem to really enjoy it. Is this a survival game, or a psy-op meant to turn ordinary video gamers into serial killers?
PvP is not that great tbh. It's not just that the combat mechanics are incomplete due to early access. Maybe the entire genre has an issue for me personally, but I found that there's almost never a fun fight. It is usually a group of high level ppl attacking a solo or lower level player. Or attacking a person's base when they are not around. Boring and pointless. Once in a while a good matchup will happen and for the 3 to 5 seconds it lasts it is fun.
I like the graphics and building. The PvE is hard to judge because it is very incomplete. NPC's do not have ai, they mostly just stand there like statues until the last moment, and then they might run off aimlessly or stand and die without fighting back. If they do react normally, they are quite easy to kite off into a corner and kill at leisure. This is true for monsters/animals as well. Even at low level you can just hop on a rock and handle almost anything. That is not necessarily horrible, since it is realistic to think that a person might take higher ground with a spear and fight off wolves or something. When i'm doing it with a dragon the size of a house... feels a bit odd :D
Finally I will mention bugs and exploits. In the PvP setting it can be very frustrating to run into people using exploits. Of course it happens in all games, (especially on Steam in my experience), but there seems to be a problem here. Bugs... yeah ok it's early access bugs are expected. You even get them in major realeases. Problem is mainly when they keep generating new bugs, and bringing back old ones that were supposedly fixed, each time they do a patch. Bugs that can make the game virtually unplayable in some cases.

In the 15+ hours that i've played this game, i've come to one simple conclusion: it is awesome and the only third person shooter worth playing.
Pros:
+loads of customization. Parts, weapons, appearance items, color schemes, expanding inventory sizes. And that's just the free version.
+friendly community. In the many rounds i've played, no one has been excessively mean spirited, but there has been some insensitive jesting. So if your feelings are made out of wet toilet paper, don't pay any attention to the chat box (not a hard task).
+Part swapping on the fly. I didn't know this till recently, but you can hit esc mid game and change your tank parts out mid match. Find yourself in a tough spot and wish you had a different setup? Wish no longer, because it's here!
+Controller support. Not something i use, but i'll list it anyway.
+Stock parts are pretty beastly! Seriously, the free parts that cost you no inventory space have the potential to be very deadly when used well.
+Set match to invites only. This allows you and your friends to blast each other away without strangers interrupting. Good for people who want to show their noob friends the ropes.
Cons:
-End of match lobby closes too quickly. There's a lobby that lets you change your setup and/or leave the match, but the next match loads too quickly for it to be of any use.
-Friend finding is inconsistent. There's a nice feature that shows you which games have your friends in them, and how many, but unfortunately the games currently open aren't always shown (maybe they don't show full matches) so i can only tell where my friends are some of the time.
-Team balancing is inconsistent. Twice in a row i've been placed 1v3 on team deathmatch.
-Some turret descriptions make it very clear that the weapons mounted on the same turret share cooldown times. However weapons mounted on different turrets do the same. Not sure if this is intentional or not, but if it is, it should say so.
Finally, it's free, so you've go nothing to lose.
I fully intend to buy the full version once i can scrape my pennies together to do so.

Forgotten Sands is a return to the style of the Sands of Time series. If you played the whole Sands of Time trilogy, and you hunger for more, Forgotten Sands will be perfect for you. If you're hoping for a new take on the franchise, you're looking in the wrong place - Forgotten Sands is not about innovation. It has the same plot and setting as every game in the Sands of Time trilogy, the same old Prince (snarky, not angsty) as ever, and the same kinds of puzzles and fights. (To be fair, the Prince gets a couple new abilities that he's never seen before to spice things up. Nothing groundbreaking, though.) However, it has refined all these so that the bad elements - quick time events, awkward chariot races, angsty Prince from the second game - have been removed and the good ones rebalanced to make them better. It is the Sands of Time trilogy with all the burrs polished away. Don't play this one first, but if you've already done the other three, Forgotten Sands is worth your time.

Zombie Vikings is an action, adventure game from Zoink Games. Let’s get rocking.
The Good
For those of you who have played and enjoyed playing Castle Crashers, I can’t stress enough that you would love Zombie Vikings. There are five playable characters, each with their own unique powers. Like Castle Crashers, any character can use any of the weapons that you unlock during the course of the game.
The artwork is incredible. It’s like Tim Burton gained a burning obsession with Norse mythology and had to draw his vision of the Nine Worlds into life. Really top notch work and very charming.
The Bad
Eh, I don’t really have any complaints about this game.
The Meh
There are no usable items to pick up in game (I.E. – Health Potions or the like) and, sometimes, it would be really nice to have them.
Most enemies take way too long to put down.
Verdict: Yea
If you’re looking for a lighthearted, darkly humorous last hurrah before Halloween comes and goes, I’d recommend picking up Zombie Vikings (maybe convince a friend or two to get a copy) and settle in for a quality good time.

Crusader Kings II is an awesome game which provided me lots of fun, but also lots of situations where I wanted to smash the PC.
You should not compare this game to any of the other Paradox titles, since it's unique in most aspects. You do not control a nation or states, you control a dynasty and characters.
There are no real states in this game, there is a pyramid of titles (Baron -> Count -> Duke -> King -> Emperor) and systems of allegiance which create "states" in this game. These states are very dynamic, as each independent Ruler has vassals. The strength of these states is mostly defined by the might of the respective ruler being king. If the ruler is a potent one, a little duchy can be quite strong. Stronger than a kingdom, which has lots of civil war going on and a weak ruler.
Characters have points in five different Skills (Diplomacy, Martial, Stewardship, Intrigue and Learning) and traits. Traits give points and relation bonusses. A just ruler is liked by his vassals, an arbitrary one contrary does not gain the favor of his vassals that easy. Traits are influenced by the education of a character and what he does (is he torturing prisoners? be prepared, you'll get the cruel trait soon.)
A good ruler has good traits and lots of points in his skills.
Very important in that period, very important in this game. Religions hate each other. Because, you know, your religion is superior. Of course. Religion enables Holy Wars, religion might benefit or crush entire empires. Put a latin catholic in charge of the Byzantine Empire and you will see what I mean. Religion can be broken down into three main branches. Christian, Muslim and "Pagan". There are Norse Paganism, Slavic Paganism, ancient Finnish beliefs, Baltic Paganism, Zoroastrians, Hinduism, Buddhism, Tengri, Judaism. All these come along with at least one heresy. Four Christian denominations (Catholics, Orthodox Christians, Nestorians, Coptic Christians) and dozens of heresys, three Muslim denominations (Ibadi, Sunni, Shia) and their respective heresies.
Diplomacy, huh? To get alliances you have to marry off your characters. Blood is thicker than water. War is basicly expansion by force. You get claims to certain titles and might makes right. Intrigue is a bit more. You can kill other characters off, plot to get them stripped of their titles, land and army or replace them as regents and so on. There's more to intrigue alone than I can described here that quick and if you'd know everything, I would spoil the fun.

Great game with intricate strategy. Provides hundreds of hours of replayability and an infinite array of possibilities of gameplay, with an incredible freedom that is characteristic of Paradox games. There are also great mods and some really nice dlcs to add to that content, although the game is pretty complete by its own. For starters in this genre of strategy games or  in Paradox games in general, Crusader Kings 2 should prove the best choice. It is not so difficult to get into and has the hole high degree of personalization of the strategy with all the rpg aspects of the game that makes some players praise it as the best game of Paradox. It is in reality a very different game from the other Paradox games such as Europa Universalis or Victoria that provides an unique kind of fun as you control the rulers instead of the nations. I personally think that despite some flaws it encompasses very well the time spam of the Middle Ages and couldn´t recommend more for any player of strategy that is fond of that period of history and of the presence of rpg elements in games in general. Finally, don´t bother with the original Crusader Kings as this one is far superior - something that is not very common nowadays with all the awful sequels we are seeing.

A moody, dark platformer where you control two seperate characters. The first character, who you control for the majority of the game, is a cat which can jump and crouch, to avoid numerous black shaded obstacles and enemies like leaping frogs, bouncing porcupines and swinging spiders.  Playing as the girl, you flip from the floor to the ceiling, to avoid trap spikes and other obstacles. The simple graphics and haunting melodies differentiate this title from the endless other indie platformers on the marketplace, but does not necessarily make it better.
Success in this game is measured in beating the 100 levels in as quick a time as possible. Destroying fragile dandelions and collecting fireflies also add to the achievement potential. I personally found the game more frustrating than enjoyable, due to the incredible difficulty on the later levels.
The game allows you to skip a certain number based on how many you have completed, leaving for some breathing space to return later, A nice touch, but not enough to raise the game above mediocrity.
A challenging platformer, those who put in the extra hours may be better rewarded for their time. Overall, a hard recommendation, but still recommended if you know what you're getting yourself into.

I don't usually write reviews, I tend to read a few of them both positive and negative before playing a game to get a general feel for what others think but then most times I jump in and play it anyway, ever watched a really good movie that "flopped" at the box office? or that critics have slated? Same thing with games, not everyone is going to enjoy it and a lot of the time what people are not liking about games is what I enjoy.
Yet reading through some of the reviews of this free game I felt compelled to add my two bits worth to the review section, namely in response to all the people complaining about "3 day install times" and "freezing crashing"
I just reinstalled this game, only have 14 hours played from before but that is because some very good games were released when I played this game first time round so it got put to the side, it took 5 minutes to install the main part of the game, yes a whole FIVE MINUTES, "OMG WTF!!111!!!!1!!" the 178.25mb update took about another 10 to 15 minutes which I will admit is slow for that size of file, it's a lot of little files in that update so it does one then has to start the other, it's not one file, so that adds to the time. if it's taken you "3 days" that is entirely down to your internet and rig, I have a fast line and a good pc, blows recomended specs out of the water, It's not the games fault that you don't have this. So your complaints are invalid, yeah I understand your frustrations yet blaming the game for your slow internet is a bit like blaming cheese for the French (no offense intended towards the beautiful country of France and it's people)
Again the "freezes and crashes" that I have seen in various reviews, I haven't experienced this, I've experienced some lag from time to time yet no different from any other online game, again probably suggests more about peoples rigs than it does the game.
Yes the graphics aren't very modern, they are servicable though, yes the controls can be a bit "clunky" still servicable though, First person seems more like an option than a requirement so I use third person more, It doesn't force you into either, yes a lot of things could be improved, same can be said for almost every game that I have played and considering that I've been palying games since before the 16k zx spectrum then I have a big back catolouge of games to compare with.
Do these things make it a bad game? Not at all, just not what everyone might be looking for, not what everyone expects when they first see this game, again personal perceptions that turn out not to be true are not the games fault, they are the players, if you expect something from the game and it turns out different, then either try something else or have a go at it without the preconceptions, Will you have fun playing it? quite possibly, if you prefer gameplay to graphics then quite probably.
A steep learning curve, yes, No "I win buttons" here, no instant success and dumbed down gaming to suit the less patient among us, I found the game to be atmospheric, immersive, challenging and rewarding, in equal measures, I see from news that there are now ingame tradable items that you can get to purchase "premium time" (Think eve's plex)
All in all for a free to play game, if you are looking for a decent experience and a game that requires half a brain cell then you might be surprised by this one.
Other things I see people complaining about that have nothing to do with the game "Chat trolls" Again no different from a large number of games that I play, there is an ignore function, the game is not responsible for people and what PEOPLE choose to do, giving a game a bad review because some PEOPLE choose to be neds is again a bit like blaming Haggis for the Scots (I'm Scottish by the way) and judging by the way the some of the people have spoken in the reviews it suggests to me that they aren't quite so squeeky clean as they believe, one of those things though.
From what I played of the game it was very good for a free game, I can't comment on end game stuff, haven't gotten that far, yet it seems that because certain people haven't been spoon fed everything right at the start and are not able to fast travel right to their quest objectives then this is somehow a wrong thing. Yes the quests require thought and things can be hard to find at first, hard to figure out, that's what a brain is for though, to think and figure things out. These same people would hate a game like Morrowind for example, where you actually have to do things yourself and think for yourself not just be pointed to everything and then have to click a mouse button a couple of times to win.
A lot of the reviews on here do not give you a good view of the game, what they give you a view of is peoples lack of patience and slow internet/rig, or a view of how people choose to act in games, they play it for an hour and see all these cool things that people who have invested in the game have and then complain because they might actually have to pay some money to it and their parents won't give them any for it, Is a game not allowed to make money?
There seems to be loads to do in the game, exploring, crafting all sorts, yes a bit clunky here and there and has issues but by no means a bad game.
No means a GREAT game either, don't get me wrong, it might not blow you away, but for what it is, I found it well worth a shot.
Edit: I've just done another couple of hours, no lag at all, no "chat trolls" and considering that there are people who have just started, not bothered to do the tutorial and stood at the start asking things like "Where do I go" "What do I do" "how do I get" "This game sucks" when all the basic game mechanics are explained with 30 seconds of reading then I have no idea where this "chat troll" stuff comes from, unless of course the people commenting this are the actual trolls as is often the case, sensible questions get answered in the help channel if folk know the answers, yet if you're not prepared to do a bit of reading and learning at the start, well again, that is not the fault of the game. It's fun.

If there's one thing that I absolutely love about this game, is that despite its learning curve can be a bit steep in terms of finding the flow of the map and then exploiting it to your advantage and then some, is that this game despite it's minimalistic look has so many moving parts that just make this work in all the right places!
Story mode is basically your standard fare fluff that shows you how the mechanics of the game work as well as getting the opportunity to unlock characters along the way as well as extra features, plus a handful of characters you can snag as DLC. In terms of animation quality, it looks like something out of your typical Saturday Morning cartoon, complete with all the cheese you can handle in terms of dialogue. But when it comes race time, it gets ruthless and in a big hurry, so you pretty much have to pull out all of the stops in order to not only keep the pace, but to also take out the competition along the way.
But what happens when you're all done with the story? Well, there's multiplayer, which you can set up a match between your friends, take on bots at different skill levels or if you're feeling brave enough, you can take on the world in ranked matchups to determine who's the fastest of them all. And the best part is, anyone who you come across are all about as skilled as you are, some may have more skill than you, but it's never unfair and evevryone is out to win as badly as you do.
In short, if you wanna win, you gotta git gud, scrub. And this is coming from someone who hasn't broke out of Entry League yet.
But in all seriousness, do I recommend this game? Sure, I do! It's perfect for those get-togethers and who want to have some fast-paced fun that may end up ruining some friendships along the way, so I wouldn't play local multiplayer unless if you're looking for a few black eyes and bloody noses.

I found out about this game\software\tool last week. I saw it come up on the Early Access "coming soon" list and was immediately excited. I, like many others, have great interest in creating games and sharing stories and adventures. However, I do not know how to code a game, all the intricate little details, changing values and so on. Because of this, titles like RPG Maker (which I've been playing since RPG Maker 2000 and beyond) have always been so appealing to me.
Then, low and behold, a 3D game that boasts that you do not have to make any line of code. Simply open the preferred editor you want and edit via a table, like the databases in the RPG Maker series. All of that sounded great, except, MANY OF THE EDITORS ARE SIMPLY BROKEN AND DO NOT WORK. I will now present a list of which editor works\functions\table comes up compared to how many do not.
Object: Yes
Terrain: Yes
Terrain Painter: Yes
Material Editor: Yes
Decal Editor: Yes
Particle Editor: Yes
River Editor: Yes
Road Editor: Yes
Mesh Road Editor: Yes, I think, I don't understand it but at least a box comes up.
Forest Editor: Yes, but I cannot spawn a single tree using it
Mission Area Editor: Yes, though no clue what this even is
Here's where things go south quickly
Weather Editor: No
Sketch Tool: No
Shape Editor: No
Attributes Editor: Yes
Tables Editor: No
Classes Editor: No
Skills Editor: No
Items Editor: No
Armors Editor: No
Weapons Editor: No
Animations Editor: No
States Editor: No
Sounds Editor: No
Terms Editor: No
Factions Editor: No
Actors Editor: No
Creatures Editor: No
Encounters Editor: No
Dialog Editor: No
Merchants Editor: No
Crafting System Editor: No
Achievements Editor: No
Events Editor: No
So out of 34 "editors," only 12 of them actually serve a function. Now what do I mean by the rest are "broken?" Well, nothing happens. When you click on "Object Editor," a table comes up that lets you edit the terrain, create grass, rock, dirt, spawn a few creatures (which most of them have no animations and just slide along the ground in a frozen state), and so on. When clicking on any editor that I listed was broken, completely nothing happens. Now, I was under the understanding that since there's no coding required, you'd make a game using all these editors. But how can you make ANYTHING when all these important editors literally have no function? You can, however, make a map with the terrain editor, which works fine and serves its purpose.
To wrap up, I can't put into words how disappointed I am. Yes, I understand this is Alpha. No, I did not expect to start making an actual game so soon after release, especially on the first day. However, I did want to look over all these promised "editors" and get a feel of what this program is capable of and is offering. I had my notepads open and ready to start brainstorming about what direction I wanted to go in as a start. However, right now, this is MyTerrain Master. Nothing else.
This is the first review I've ever done for a game because I'm that passonate for game making that I want to let everyone know what they're getting into. No possible game can come from this. Not right now anyway. Stay away for now and wait for updates.
EDIT: I've actually found 2 more editors, one of them is broken and one of them seems to do something. Social Network Editor is broken and Datablock Editor seems to function.
EDIT 2: The developers have finally (after they got some of our money) talked about all the missing features this game currently has, which you can read here:
I highly suggest you read that post over before you consider buying this. This is shady behavior from developers and a real quick way to get some of their fanbase turned against them.

Cradle is a mystery sci-fi puzzle game. The story and world is intriguing and can give your creativity a refreshing jolt, overall the story is the best part about this game but it is a bit short (about 10 hours gametime).
The ending leaves you with a lot of questions, reading the hidden "Babylonian effect" logs(have a look at the achivements guide) as well as all the other scattered bits of information helps fill in the gaps but ultimatley what really happened is still left open to interpretation, if you like such a story than this game is for you.
The hardest part to clear is the start, after that it gets easier as you start interacting with voiced characters and become famililar with the interface. The voice acting itself is satisfying except for one irritant, the voice audio cuts out a bit prematurely on some dialogues.  There is a vast open world but this is mostly for scenery as the only things worth finding are between the house and the amusement park. Most of the game is rendered realistically but the sky is rendered artistically, this becomes most clear at night when constellations and some sort of pictographs are projected onto the sky.
There is also a forced mini-game which is actually quite good but not everyone likes being forced to play mini-games.
Finally dont worry about misplacing items in the world, it gets reset after each quest so it cant get lost. Most of the newspaper snippets laying around everywhere are non-essential so you dont need to try reading all of them but they do help clear up the mystery.
This game is like that game your Dad bought you because he thought it was cool and you play and it sucks but your too scared of telling your dad so you just smile and pretend to like it.

This is the most invested into a story and characters in a very long time.
Story:  The story really drew me in.  It won't win any awards and seems a little stretched thin at times, however, I took my time with this one ready all the little notes in drawers and on tables and it really "filled out" the game world.
Characters:  I got kind of attached to Ida which surprised me I didn't expect to get so invested in her. The voice acting was great and maybe it was the use of actual footage of actors eye movements but the 2 npcs in the game felt very human...
Music:  Was perfect for this game.  Although one song stood out and was really out of place and another was so beautiful I just stood outside and listened to the music fo a while.
Graphics:  The graphics where excellent and the art style is one of the most impressive I've seen.  It really serves to pull you in and make you feel as though you are in an actual place not just a game.
TL:DR
The art the music and the way the game gets you to invest yourself into the writing and characters are its strong point. If you like to take your time and be absorbed in your games then this one may be for you.  Taking it slow and reading all the articles, posters, and newspaper clippings around fill in the blanks with the story but they are optional.  If you get stuck press TAB for subtle hints on what to do.

In Brief:  It's Rust meets Swords & Sorcery, and it's great fun.  (although, being in alpha, sorcery has yet to be implemented.)  I woke up and started running naked through the desert.  Just an average thursday, other than the giant anthropomorphic bat creature stooped over the still-bleeding corpse of a roman centurion, who is missing his left leg from just above the knee.  It's going to be one of THOSE days.  Picked up a few rocks, tied them to a stick.  In no time I'm stripping bark from trees, when sweet lord, some mutant flesh goblin is gnawing on my gonads.  A few good whacks later, he's dead on the ground and I'm harvesting his flesh and skin for my own use.  10 hours later I've finally finished my sandstone fortress, have 2 slaves who cook for me, I've been eaten by crocodiles twice, fell to my death from a cliff, gotten stabbed by a voodoo shaman whose mojo stick hurt more than it looks like it should, and I'm having a blast.
High points and low points:
--Survival mechanics: 5/10 - Passable.  Basic hunger/thirst only.  Really wish they'd add more of an exposure element, especially considering how terribly hot the whole landscape LOOKS.  Could use a more in-depth clothing system, Heat/Cold, etc.  RIght now it seems that exposure simply makes you thirsty quicker.  But I was playing a fair-skinned nordic character in the desert.  Considering how good the graphics are (see below) it felt wrong not to be horribly sunburned, or at least sweating.  Most fans of the genre know that exposure is one of your main problems in an actual survival situation, moreso than hunger or thirst.  I feel it deserves more than just lip-service from a survival game.    Harvesting and crafting happens at a good pace.  Construction of tools and other objects feels realistically difficult and in a "just right" zone.
--Combat mechanics: 4/10 - Think Skyrim.  For you Bethesda lovers, the reason I call this a 4 is that this game truly suffers from a lack of Mount & Blade-esque melee combat: directional attacks & blocks, momentum, etc.  For a game that uses Conan the friggin Barbarian as its namesake, I would expect more options as to HOW I dismember my opponents, rather than simply running up to them and clicking alot.  At the moment, it doesn't seem like hit location is even a thing - a blow to the shin is as good as a blow to the head.  Ever since "Barbarian" was released for the Commodore 64 in 1988, a blow to the neck meant decapitation in this genre, regardless of HP.  Combat should not be getting dull in a Conan game.
--Base Mechanics: 9/10 - Very much fun, and purposeful.  Construction is tight and fairly bug-free.  For a game that is not voxel-based, ala minecraft or 7 Days to Die, there are a surprising number of options.  This is one of the best and most engaging aspects of the game, in my opinion.  I'm also glad they implemented a "ruins" system which gradually destroys buildings that receive no upkeep, otherwise a server with lots of players would very quickly fill up with player-made bases that never decay.  They've also just implemented siege warfare in the latest patch, which is an interesting development...
--Character Progression: 10/10 - the game unlocks new content to you at an excellent pace.  All the skills you learn as you level are interesting and useful and there are skills for every playstyle.  There's also too much to learn on your own, which really encourages cooperation: having a town blacksmith, carpenter, leatherworker, dedicated warriors, etc.  I have nothing bad to say about it.
--Game World & Gameplay 9/10:  This place is HUGE and there are lots of interesting things to see, explore, and kill.  A plethora of different environments, creatures, dungeons, huge and dangerous boss monsters, etc.  The sandstorms are truly terrifying.  You can enslave NPC humans and turn them into "thralls," essentially stocking your base with "citizens" who work for you as archers, warriors, blacksmiths, cooks, etc.  Again, this is all doled out at an excellent pace.
--Graphics & Sound 8/10: The SHADOWS and lighting are striking, and utterly realistic.  Seeing a shadow cast on me at sunset from a tree on a cliff 300+ meters above is truly impressive.  I don't have a high-end machine, and the graphics are still gorgeous.  Still some glitchy animations, particularly on NPC's & monsters.  The blood spatter says a hyena is biting me, but the animation shows him lounging in the sun and facing the other direction.  I imagine this will improve as the development progresses.  The orchestrations are lovely, the ambient music is appropriate.  Although, the stirring combat music which clicks in the moment a monster notices you also ensures that its only possible to be surpised by an attack from another player.
--OVERALL:  7.5/10:  I'm having a lot of fun with this game, but it has its flaws.  I could forgive the dumbed-down survival mechanics a bit more if they overhauled the combat system.  And to be fair, I could probably forgive the lackluster combat system a bit more if they improved the survival mechanics.  The elements they are planning to implement all sound great: social emotes, sorcery, human sacrifice, and other great Barbarian-y things.  Highly recommended to fans of the genre, but for it to become truly great, I do hope we get a bit of a deeper system for either fighting or staying alive.  Or preferably, both.  Right now, it feels like a game about building castles and enslaving the masses.  Which is fine, but the game is called "Conan Exiles."  To me, that title indicates the focus should be on dismemberment and wasteland survival.

The best way too describe Zombie Vikings in a nutshell, is to imagine playing as a cutesy Viking character inside of a trippy story-driven brawler cartoon. One with a decidely groovy feel showcasing a plethora of wacky monsters to battle against, replete with an abundance of quirky stoner-esque humour of the British variety. In fact you'll have your choice of 4 very different characters to play as (Gunborg, Seagurd, Hedgy and Caw-kaa) at any point in your progression of the game, each with their own uniquely distinctive attacks and personalities.
Developed & published by Zoink Games as a worthy successor to their previous hit title "Stick It to The Man!", the game capitalizes on exceptionally impressive artwork and creativity in its presentation...it's definite strong suit here.
Dialogue, written by Zach Weinersmith from SMBC Comics, is top-notch and will be sure to have you laughing out loud in no time at all. The flavour of which can only be described as witty and absurdist in scope...fitting seamlessly right into this style of cartoony game. Best of all, it can be enjoyed by gamers of all ages and is very accesible. Just about anyone can pick up and play this in no time at all.
The premise of this game is that an evil trickster named Loki has stolen Odin's good eye...the grandfatherly figure in the game who possesses "the sparkliest staff in all of Valhalla". And so Odin recruits a Viking posse to help him retrive his missing eye. As such, you are one of these sword-wielding warriors who must assist him across the span of 25 levels (which include side-missions)...equipped with both a primary as well as secondary special attack (both of which can be powered up further by holding down their respective buttons to alter the attack into a more powerful form).
Furthermore, there are countless weapon types to unlock as well as you progress further in. The entire combat system is actually quite impressive, with many various abilities and moves to master...it's quite rich in that regard. Best of all, you can simply play it as a frantic button masher and hope for the best (which works suprisingly well I might). Or you can actually master the nuances of each individual maneuver with practice, honing & fine-tuning your skills for maximum effectiveness.
Gameplay isn't terribly difficult nor frustrating fortunately, found somewhere between casual and competitive...just about right for the widest range of audience. And along the way, you will be collecting gold coins and health from smashed wooden boxes scattered everywhere within the levels, the former of which can be used inside the in-game shop to purchase weapon upgrades as desired.
I was extremely impressed with the art style in particular here...it's easily some of the best I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing in a 2.5D game such as this one. And even if the gameplay wasn't up to par (which thankfully it is)...you'd still be hard-pressed not to appreciate the game purely for the aesthetic beauty of its creatively inspired levels, characters, and cut-scenes. It certainly resonated with me immediately.
Thankfully all aspects of its audio were very strong in calibre. The soundtrack is one comprised of a very groovy sounding 60's/70s style, the kind that I wish I heard much more of in modern video games actually. Whereas sound effects were of high quality and well-chosen to match the very light-hearted & highly humourous atmosphere of this title. Lastly, and perhaps most impressive of all, the voice acting here is simply stellar...clearly done by professionals who know their craft well. This was definitely a breath of fresh air compared to many other such games which suffer in this one particular area.
It fully is, and includes both trading cards and 34 achievements to be unlocked.
There are 3 available DLC's for Zombie Vikings, comprising of 2 individual character packs (Frostbjörn & Raybjörn) plus a soundtrack. These are however very much optional add-ons for those who are true fans of the game.
Zombie Vikings is a superbly designed game that I truly wanted to rate substantially higher, because the actual game itself is phenomenal in so many wonderful ways...with it's exceptionally brilliant dialog, high-quality voice-acting, stellar artwork presentation, trippy/groovy music and sound effects, quirky humour, as well as its sheer creative prowess. But technically, the game simply doesn't run as well and as silky smooth as it should - even on powerful & modern hardware....whereby the framerate will gyrate considerably and where its scrolling is unusually choppy. Thus it clearly suffers from optimization issues which must be addressed urgently. Coupled with some glaring bugs such as option adjustments not being properly saved...I unfortunately have no choice but to demerit this game some points for the purpose of this review. Hopefully the developer can release a future patch which addresses these concerns...and I do believe that a forthcoming one is planned by what I hear. But as of right now however...
I'll rate this one a 7.5/10
...with a possible revision higher at a later date if warranted.
- Gorgeous 2.5D artwork, some of the best you'll find in a brawler
- Selectable cutesy characters and a diverse assortment of unique enemies
- 40 unlockable weapons + shop system
- Remappable keys
- Skippable cut-scenes
- Nice amount of adjustable graphics options
- Up to 4-player co-op + online/offline multiplayer
- Steam achievements + trading cards
- Full controller support
- Definite optimization issues, runs a bit choppy
- A bug where some settings reset each time you start the game

A truly fantastic game, which deserves much more attention than it got.
Top-notch, gorgeous to look at hand-drawn graphics. You can practically make some screenshots during cutscenes and choose any of them as your wallpaper, they're THAT good. Never wanted to skip a single cutscene (skipped only if needed to replay the level again). It's like watching a cartoon, a really good one.
The levels are extremely detailed and unique, never felt like going through the same thing all over again.
A guy stole the Odin's Eye from Odin himself and Odin sent four zombie vikings to bring the eye back. The premise is pretty simple but the result is the massive adventure and story which never takes itself seriously. I'd actually compare it to South Park, but I liked Zombie Vikings more than South Park (and in my opinion it's more funnier). The jokes are both stupid and clever, but they work, definitely work. ZV actually would make a great series rather than being just a game.
Just as amazng as artwork. The music has its own unique flavour. The mix of jazz, rock'n'roll, rockabilly, bassy ambientish tunes, etc. The music feels right and never out of place, absolutely fits the game.
The voice acting is superb. The characters feel alive and overall the way they should be, not a single miscast. A really wonderful job, every single character is pleasant to listen.
It's a beat'em'up, but much more co-op oriented than the games from 90s. You can play it alone, but I'd not recommend to do that. It's not necessarily to gather a party of four, just one friend would be fine. The game doesn't have online matchmaking and you can only invite friends. You don't share coins and health drops between each other, so you need to decide who gets what on the fly (also, there's no in-game chat).
The game itself is simple, but fun to play and doesn't get old or boring. By progressing further you unlock new weapons (sometimes you fight with other players to decide who gets the free weapon) and runes. They can bring new things to gameplay or even change the way you play. You don't really need to spend a single coin, which I think is great because it makes the game more balanced (skill matters more than power of your weapons). If some weapon has more damage, you'll also get  less HP for equipping it.
It's actually a long game (especially for its genre), maybe way too long. Despite the length, the pacing is right and there's always something new on the way.
On top of that, there are also many side quests and you may miss something along your way. You can always return to a level to finish the side quest, which is great.
The performance is stable, there were no FPS drops, crashes or freezes.
But I did encounter bugs, two of them forced us to replay the level. The first time we stuck while playing as a giant (literally stuck and weren't able to move around), the second time was the enemy not moving from outside the screen (actually something like that was also before).
A unique, criminally underrated game, feels and plays like a cult classic. Absolutely recommended.

I first played Jet Set Radio on the SEGA Dreamcast back when the game was first released. I had fond memories of it from back then and so I was keen to add it to my Steam collection when it came out on PC.
Sadly, I have found that just like my hazy memories of childhood cartoons, those of Jet Set Radio were somewhat rose tinted. The game certain still looks good thanks to the bold colour selection and cell-shaded graphics. But the game itself is nowhere near as fun as I seemed to recall.
The major issue with the game is the sense of movement from the character. Remember, that here the characters are supposed to be ‘super-cool’ skater/punk/rebels that zoom around Tokyo-to on their powered inline-skates. Indeed, this game is all about movement. Yet it utterly fails to deliver on this front.
The character moves slowly and there is never a sense of inertia from the roller skates. Moving around feels more like wading in treacle than skating. It’s virtually impossible to get any real momentum up at all.
This was made very clear in an early level where the character starts in a half-pipe area. There are locations to tag at the top of either side. My first instinct was to get some momentum up going back and forth in the pipe in order to perform the graffiti tags mid-air. But it’s not possible since there is no speed gain from coming down the steep slope. The character just grinds to a halt at the bottom. Tony Hawks Pro Skater this is not…
That the movement is so poor is really strange given that this game is all about movement. Yet rather than letting me feel cool by pulling of speedy moves I ended up feeling more like Chris from Resident Evil using a pair of Fisher Price my-first-skates.
Also, I’d add that given the game chooses to focus its plot around a radio station, it might have been nice if they had put a little more effort into the sound-track. As it stands it’s like skating to an album of B-sides from Parappa the Rapper on the PS1.
And so there we go. It’s a game that I once loved but time has not been kind to it. The movement is terrible and the soundtrack is just as bad. It’s all the more annoying as I am sure there is a fun game in here somewhere. But as it stands the strange design choices manage to quash any spark of joy before it gets going.

5/10 Tengami is a point and click adventure game. The one distinction is that it is in the form of a japanese pop-up paper book. The art style of the game is very cool, and is the only redeeming feature, along with the relaxing japanese music. The game is very relaxing. But it almost doesn't even feel like a game, just a meditative experience or a piece of artwork. Since I am reviewing it as a game, there isn't much positive to say. The ability to flip up or down things is fun and inventive at first, but is all the game uses as a mechanic. You spend the whole gaming clicking on your guy to walk around, basically making this a walking simulator. He moves super slowly, and there is no way to get him to run or speed up, meaning you spend 1/3 of the game just waiting for him to slowly meandor to where you clicked him to go, which is super boring.
Most point and clicks, since their gameplay is pretty basic, boring, and repetitive, rely on great characters, stories, conversation choices, etc. Tengami has none of those. There is no story, conversation, or characters, besides the mute guy you control. You collect and use a few things, and solve a few random puzzles that don't seem to make much sense. The adventure mechanic is also kind of wonky. You walk to preset areas highlighted to flip the scene or an object. The problem is, is sometimes this area is highlighted, and other times it is not until you stand at a certain spot. This means some parts you get lost, because you didn't know you had to walkt to the end of that random dock so that then an object for you to use would be highlited to flip, or then an are would become highlited to walk to. Also, some parts, the progression makes no sense. You will have walked to a new scene, do something, and then you're supposed to know you need to go back 2 scenes, flip something, do a puzzle there, then go forward to that other scene, flip it, and do something, all to go to this other place. The lack of direction/story means theres a lot of wandering around since there is no real story objective or thing to do.
As mentioned towards the end of above, there is a lot of backtracking and walking back and forth through the same places, and since he moves slowly, it just adds frustration, which isn't ideal for a "relaxing" game. Finally, there is the length. The game takes a little over an hour, with nothing memorable besides maybe a boat ride with cool sounds. The novel idea of the flipbook and the good music lose their luster early, and then the poor game is all that is left. Watch a youtube playthrough or look at pictures of the game,  you'll see what you need to without wasting money and time playing this.

That should be a good game : Super Meat Boy + VVVVVV + a runner game, all 3 gameplays alternately, whao !
To put it simply, playing cat is sometimes a runner+VVVVVV, sometimes SMB, and playing girl is VVVVVV
Let's begin by the good points then :
+ 2/3 of the game are alternatively SMB and VVVVVV, (wonder if I should put it here, because it lacks originality)
+ last tier of the game is more creative, because of the mix between VVVVVV and runner
+ good soundtracks, and pretty nice background (which is also a bad point here)
+ like in SMB, you respawn fast
+ good diversity of levels
+ and ... that's all !
Now, the bad points (ouch, so many ?) :
For the SMB like :
-inertia is far too strong : impossible to do a small jump, and when you stop running, you will need a little time to start again in full gear (this holds true for jumps, too). This is such a pain when you need to do precise moves or jumps,and especially wall-jumps, or steering in mid-air
- edges of platforms are buggy, and you will sometimes freeze for no reason, or being unable to jump
- due to the very bright background, you often can't see well things that are white and shining (such as trinkets or gravity reversers). This holds true for the whole game.
- timings of saws/platforms makes them often in the way of your progression, and you need to stop (and loose your speed, of course), this kills the pleasure of a fast run/fast death/fast respawn
For the girl (VVVVVV like) :
- still the same problem with inertia, but as you don't need to jump, it's not as painful
This is by far the most playable mode.
For the runner like :
- whenever you lag, you're dead (and to me it happened a lot of times at any time, maybe because of my comp)
- a STUPID achievement requires to win each of these levels in the "first run", meaning that if you want to finish the levels at 100%, then whenever you die, it's ESC -> go back to map -> reload the level (restart won't give you the "first run"), which is a dumb concept for a fast respawn runner.
It's not really what I would call a bad game, but due to the several points I mentioned, it kills fun. All that remains is frustration, piling up in all the levels, and the will to finish at 100% this addictive game (when you respawn, the game automatically begins, so you hardly have a second to breath or to get out of it), and all of this for what ? to see that you will NEVER finish it at 100 % when you witness the last challenge level (I've tackled it for half an hour and I always die after the first seconds, and the levels are awfully long).
Well, this review is certainly quite long too, so I will end it here :
This is NOT a new SMB and NOT a new VVVVVV, because I don't want to compare a jewel to a rock

I'll start by saying I enjoyed it and for the $2 I payed for it the game is nice. However, I'd never pay $20. I can only recommend getting it during a huge sale.
Graphics
The graphics are nice enough, but unpolished. They remind me of early PS3 fare. There's a lot of weird clipping that goes on but there's nothing game-breaking.
Atmosphere
This is the purpose of the game and I think it pulls it off well. I quickly got the sense of the environment and backdrop which actually let me guess the story without more than a couple "secrets". It's eerie and calming at the same time.
Gameplay
Repetitive but calming, so it fits in the game's overall theme. Gameplay consists of boating and climbing up/down ledges and pipes. That's pretty much it.
Story
Nearly non-existent but there's definitely enough there to intrigue me. Unfortunately the game sets up a world with an intriguing past, an interesting present and a tenuous future then does nothing with it. Your actions are ultimately insignificant and rather pointless in the grand scheme of things. This along with the tiny playtime are the huge negatives for me.
Game Length
Tiny. 2 hours is what it took for me to unlock half the achievements, beat the game and find over half of the secrets. If you wanted to you could easily beat the game and still be able to refund it.
So again, it's worth it if you want a sedate, short exploration game. Just get it on a big sale.

Crusader Kings II is an awesome game which provided me lots of fun, but also lots of situations where I wanted to smash the PC.
You should not compare this game to any of the other Paradox titles, since it's unique in most aspects. You do not control a nation or states, you control a dynasty and characters.
There are no real states in this game, there is a pyramid of titles (Baron -> Count -> Duke -> King -> Emperor) and systems of allegiance which create "states" in this game. These states are very dynamic, as each independent Ruler has vassals. The strength of these states is mostly defined by the might of the respective ruler being king. If the ruler is a potent one, a little duchy can be quite strong. Stronger than a kingdom, which has lots of civil war going on and a weak ruler.
Characters have points in five different Skills (Diplomacy, Martial, Stewardship, Intrigue and Learning) and traits. Traits give points and relation bonusses. A just ruler is liked by his vassals, an arbitrary one contrary does not gain the favor of his vassals that easy. Traits are influenced by the education of a character and what he does (is he torturing prisoners? be prepared, you'll get the cruel trait soon.)
A good ruler has good traits and lots of points in his skills.
Very important in that period, very important in this game. Religions hate each other. Because, you know, your religion is superior. Of course. Religion enables Holy Wars, religion might benefit or crush entire empires. Put a latin catholic in charge of the Byzantine Empire and you will see what I mean. Religion can be broken down into three main branches. Christian, Muslim and "Pagan". There are Norse Paganism, Slavic Paganism, ancient Finnish beliefs, Baltic Paganism, Zoroastrians, Hinduism, Buddhism, Tengri, Judaism. All these come along with at least one heresy. Four Christian denominations (Catholics, Orthodox Christians, Nestorians, Coptic Christians) and dozens of heresys, three Muslim denominations (Ibadi, Sunni, Shia) and their respective heresies.
Diplomacy, huh? To get alliances you have to marry off your characters. Blood is thicker than water. War is basicly expansion by force. You get claims to certain titles and might makes right. Intrigue is a bit more. You can kill other characters off, plot to get them stripped of their titles, land and army or replace them as regents and so on. There's more to intrigue alone than I can described here that quick and if you'd know everything, I would spoil the fun.
To summarize. This is a Grand Strategy Game of Intrigue, Warfare, Love, Chivalry. You could describe it as Strategic Medieval Character Simulation. The entire franchise is reduced very often, you should buy everything, when it's 75% off, since it is very expensive at the regular price. These are just some aspects of the game. Have a look for yourself when the game's reduced. I hope this was somewhat helpful.
