Recap: Tanki X, a game by AlternativaPlatform, is a game built off the scrapped idea of Tanki 2.0. The original game is Tanki Online(TO), an online browser Tank Action Arena game, where you can join lobbies, of which is based on rank, to play Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture The Flag, Control Points and rarely event gamemodes.
Features: Let's move onto Tanki X itself. This game is taking a different direction than TO. At the very start you play with the original Smoky turret and Hunter hull, and you battle in Training Battles where you play against bots. After you obtain enough mastery and crystals to upgrade both the hull and turret, you will be able to choose a gamemode (SIDENOTE: when I was a VERY low rank, regardless of mastery, I had to keep playing random games to rank up and later be able to choose a gamemode, so it may have changed.) From here, the process pretty much is earning score to rank up, earn mastery, and earn crystals to unlock, upgrade, and expiriment with Turrets and Hulls. There are 101 ranks from Novice Recruit to Legend. Tanki X uses a great balancing system, Effective Level, which is the rank used in match-making to pair you up with others that have similar Effective Levels and what it is: The lowest upgrade # of your turret or hull equipped +1 IF one is greater than another, otherwise it is just the same upgrade #. In place of supplies, Tanki X uses 'Modules', which are powerups that can be used any number of times based on a cooldown. One of the last things I want to mention is containers, they are basically crates you buy with X-crystals to recieve cosmetics, ranging from 65-850 X-crystals. X-crystals, crystals, and containers can be obtained from missions (Common > Rare: Crystals, X-Crystals, Containers) X-Crystals can be bought with IRL currency.
How do I think of the game?: Overall, it's a great improvement of TO. I want to share my opinion of the Great features, and the bad things of Tanki X.
First the good parts: Tanki X has beautiful graphics even on the lowest settings. A fair matchmaking system, Effective Level. Anti-Pay-To-Win. An option to obtain premium currency (X-Crystals) through missions. Cosmetics which can be bought with X-Crystals, the premium currency. Great selection of turrets and hulls. Gamemodes to suit your preference. Active, growing community. Free to play.
In my opinion, these are some bad parts of the game: Lack of Control Points (a gamemode). Some gamebreaking bugs, such as the one recently forcing some players not to play a certain gamemode. MIssion rewards and CTF (Capture The Flag) rewards are small compared to TDM (Team Deathmatch) rewards. Some Hulls and Turrets can be unbalanced compared to one another. Server funding isn't perfect (Tanki Online has better servers because the game and its dev team are ten years old and much money and time was invested into the servers, unlike Tanki X servers and Development team, which are 1 year experienced) Doesn't have a lobby / Battle select based system as like the one in To where you could play with friends, and choose your teams. Lack of communication in Tanki X.

A belated review.
There are two games around the same time put out there that want to take on the Dungeon Keeper gameplay, Dungeons 2 and War for the Overworld. Frankly, and after actually playing through it again recently, neither take DK2 off its throne and even now Id recommend getting a copy of that first.
(Though keep in mind that there is now a Dungeons 3 that may have superceded all of them.)
but the closest to it is Dungeons 2 and thats because it innovates, it takes out some of the clunky bits of DK and replaces it with a more sensical (Though rough around the edges) adventure mode. War for the Overworld may seem to innovate at first, there is an awful lot thrown in, but also an awful lot of it is quite redundant, and at its core it _feels_ like a DK2 mod with a less compelling campaign, and a lot of annoying timed levels.
Almost all thats good in the game is taken nearly verbatim from the Dungeon Keeper series, then there are a bunch of additions some of which seemed unnecessary, some of which I dont think I ever even needed to use. Rather than throw in all that, Id much rather have seen an attempt at some real changes in mechanics and gameplay. Or at least make levels compelling enough not to need to add timed events to so many of them. Im not playing an e-sport I wanted to take my time, and timers are a _very_ lazy way of introducing challenge that wasnt even all that necessary. (Or for that matter that challenging anyway, it isnt a particularly hard game.)
I actually kickstarted this game and I dont hugely regret that, the developers have made a mostly decent game that does what it says on the tin and I hope to see more, and more interesting games from them. Id probably give it a neutral review if I could, but as it stands I ended up fairly bored and sometimes frustrated once the nostalgia fell away.
Ultimately Id rather take flawed and new over a flawed clone, and in a way, the inovation of the alternative is more in keeping with what Dungeon Keeper was doing than this much closer copy of its game play.

You like:
- complex crafting
- open worlds
- classless character progression
- postapocalyptic setting
- manual targeting
You don't expect:
- a very colorful cheerful game
- a set on rails progression
- next-gen graphics
If this fits to what you like, then you will most likely like this game. The crafting is great, the graphics are in some ways not so good (character animations), in some ways average (character models), in some ways really nice (for example having a huge view over the open landscape during a sunset).
It's definately not for everyone, but I enjoyed it a lot and played it a lot. The community is friendly and helpful too. There are a lot of factions, an ongoing storyline, and you often have "what is behind that hill" moments. And Fallen Earth lets you find out what is behind that hill. There are no invisible walls (except that you can't enter water, of which there is not much to begin with).
I think the game is very relaxing, when you ride over the open landscape and look forward to have your next crafting items finished (crafting can be done while you are offline or doing other stuff), and at times intense, when you are stuck in a cave full of spiders and slowly running out of ammo.

is a racing side-scrolling platform video game, where your objective is to guide an avatar around an interative environment as quickly as possible so as to force your opponents to trail off-screen, thereby eliminating them from the competition.
The availability of a single-player campaign in addition to local and online mutliplayer coupled with the application of Bushnell's law (i.e., easy to learn, difficult to master) provides engaging, addictive, and approachable gameplay at all competitive levels. Despite a tediously repetitive single-player campaign, the multiplayer experience offers replayability, which is in largle part due to the role luck plays in a race, achievements and leaderboards as well as unlockable characters.
The minimalistic visuals are unimpressive but appropriate, as the continuous movement does not allow prolonged observation. Additionally, the simplicity serves to increase the identifiability of the mechanics of each map, a crucial aspect to the successful navigation of a racing track. High-tempo audio tracks in conjunction with sound effects produce an immersive impression, which is neccesary to elicit faults through emphatic pressure, advancing the outcome of a race.
A recommended title for casual, fun, and multiplayer gameplay.

He's smug, vain, arrogant and somewhat rude. Yet the world just can't seem to get enough of him. Even Agatha Christie couldn't stand him. In fact,
as a “detestable, bombastic, tiresome, ego-centric little creep.” And
other authors about creating a character like this in an essay from 1930. He was however a creep that made her a lot of money given his popularity, so she was stuck with him.
During the war though, she made a plan to ensure his death should she herself die. Yep, she wanted to ensure that he could not live on if she didn't. Yikes. She wrote the story about his (and Miss Marple's) death in 1945, with instructions to publish if she got killed.
She survived, as did her detectives, and she continued to produce stories about them for another 30 years. Until her own health started to fail in the 1970s, and she finally decided to kill him (cause of death:
). The public reaction was intense,
(this was the first time a fictional character had gotten an obituary) - no doubt to Christie's annoyance. She died the year after, ensuring that no one would continue to write new stories about the ego-centric little creep she had created several decades earlier.*
That never stopped anyone from creating new versions of existing stories - the most famous adaptation is probably the
that aired from 1989 to 2013. And then there's this game, based on the novel with the same name from 1936. In other words, if you have read that novel (or watched that episode), you already know the plot. If not, I'm not gonna spoil it here anyway.
This is a fairly standard point and click mystery adventure, where in addition to actually solving the mystery you get bonus points for behaving like Poirot would. The point system is aptly called "ego-points", and one of the things you can do to gain them is to make sure you look at yourself (and groom your 'stache) everytime you're near a mirror. In short, they have captured his spirit. Props for that. I also think there's just a right amount of complicated puzzles, and it has a certain hook to it. I enjoyed connecting the dots (or as he would say, getting the little grays to work), and sorting through relevant information and red herrings.
I do however find it a bit of an uneccessarily slow game. It's point and click, and you have to wait for the animation, or more accurately, Poirot himself. You have to wait for him to walk places, to finish talking, and so on. I'd maybe have more patience for that if I liked him more.** There's actually an achievement for getting impatient with him. There is, of course, no doubt that he is good at his job. As are you if you manage to solve the mysteries at hand. And by the way you will, don’t worry. There’s not actually any way to fail at this game I think? But you might find yourself spending time on the puzzles, sometimes due to the animation of it dragging out, but sometimes because they’re complex.
So I'm sorry Agatha, but I'm going to recommend this game to people who enjoy point-and-click-puzzles.

Bardbarian is a tower defence game with a unique twist, the towers are attached to the main character and you steer them around the battlefield to take out the creeps.
There are elements from many games here, the lane approach of Plants vs. Zombies, the grind and slowly improve of many IAP games and even playing guitar riffs like in Brutal Legend to buff your group.  The cartoon graphics are beautiful and the various towers look great.
You troops come in many familiar variants, from glass cannon ninjas to de-buffing Shaman to front line tanks and healers.  There are even some familiar faces from the Indie world that make an appearance!  There is a decent amount of strategy in the choice but you can only bring 3 types of towers at a time, I can't help but think if this limit was relaxed it would have provided a more interesting game.  It is increased to 4 after you complete the game once but still...
You can be constantly on the move, attack from angles with high damage low health units to attacking front on with the tank taking the damage while shooing down lanes or even some variation thereof.  I used a front line of ninjas with shamans and an engineer to provide support.  Looking around there does seem to be a nice variation of viable builds, a definite plus!
The grind is the biggest issue here and shows the games IAP roots.  Taking out IAP and just making the game paid for the PC market does not a great game make, it seems as though the grind is the primary game mechanism at times, not fun.  There is only one map in the main game and even though every 5 levels out of the the total of 20 the time of day changes and you get a unique boss, there is no discernible difference apart from slightly different creeps.  There are a couple of other modes, survival where creeps come from all angles and and escape mode where you navigate a maze of creeps and obstacles to see how far you go.
There are a few cosmetic bugs, but nothing major and I'm sure they will get patched at some point.
If steam reviews had a “meh” category this game would fall into it.  It's too grindy for a paid game and doesn't really offer enough value for it's price.  Pick it up in a bundle or on sale and wile away a few hours or don't!

Been following this game for however long it's been in development and it really has met my expectations and even exceeded them to some extent. The adventure-ish gameplay is well done and there's essentially no handholding outside some "hints" that act more like journal entries than actual hints and the environment is pretty interactable. An issue I have with it though is that it's often hard to accurately place items if you want to put them in various places because most items are held too close to the character and there's also no rotate key. There's tons of things to read and character dialogue (and your character is voiced, which is a strange choice as well) to flesh out the background and make the world even more mysterious and interesting.
I've only played one of the minigames so far but it's shakes up the gameplay a bit. It can pretty quickly turn into a platforming nightmare if you start running out of blocks to stand on. The ability to skip these if you fail once though is a pretty strange choice.
The graphics are great too. Texture quality is pretty amazing for an indie game that costs $13 and so is pretty much everything else.
The bad however is that the game utterly fails on the technical options. Outside of texture quality, resolution, and vsync there's only a "quality" slider which goes from 1 to 10 so you can't really adjust individual options. There's also no way to rebind keys, which seems unthinkable for a PC game. No fov options either, and while I don't really get bothered by lov fov some people do. The lack of graphics options also isn't helped by the game potentially not being too well optimized. And even if it's just one option being pushed too far rather than lack of optimization, there's no way to individually adjust this option or even test to see what it is.
So yeah, overall the game is highly recommended for the game part as it has a decent bit of variety and mostly accomplishes what it sets out to do pretty well. The bizzare lack of common PC features though is a pretty large oversight and I have no idea how anyone of the devs thought "yes, this is a good state to release the game in". Hoping for some patches in the future to fix these things.

This game should be a ROLE MODEL for the entire gaming industry.
I have never seen:
A game change as much since its launch;
Devs respecting players as much;
A game doing GRIND right;
A F2P game be THIS well done and open for anyone that doesn't want to spend a dime on it;
A game/community that welcomes new players this well;
And, most importantly, never seen a company try this f*cking hard to break the limits.
The only things that hold back this game from being ♥♥♥♥ing legendary in all aspects of the word is the PVP and hardcore endgame shiz.
Since the game's movement is very frenetic and has always been about PVE, the PVP does not work that well and very few people play it (it's not the type of game that will feel lackluster without it tho).
There are raids in this game but nothing very close to what other mmorpgs call hardcore raiding... However, I do believe that sometime in the future, the devs will look into that and I'm damn eager for that to happen!
BUT,
If you hear someone say that the game is too much grind or that everything takes too long to get, IT'S A GOD DAMN LIE.
By LONG TIME TO GET they mean you LITERALLY have to wait for items to craft (which can take from 1 minute to 24 hours, excluding frames, which take 72), but that will NEVER hold back your progress. "Taking a long time to get" in other games mean that you have to tryhard big time for a long time until you achieve your goal, but not in Warframe.
NOTHING in this game is hard to get (from the perspective of a ex-semi-hardcore raider in other MMOs), all you have to do is get materials sometimes if you didn't get enough while you naturally progressed, which doesn't take 40 minutes if the item requires a LOT of♥♥♥♥♥♥
The "CASH" currency in this game is tradeable and DE (the devs) made it so you can ONLY trade plat (the cash currency) and not credits or other ingame currencies. If you know other MMOs, you know that items that are worth "real money" are usually the ones that are top tier endgame shiz, right? In Warframe that is completely wrong. The list of "high tier" and viable weapons in this game is IMMENSE when compared to other games and you can get most of these weapons ANYTIME. The things that you actually sell in this game are mods and primed parts (you'll find out what they are on your own). You get primed parts by cracking relics on void fissure missions. Oh, what are them and how hard are them to get/crack? STUPID EASY is the answer, because there are 4 types of relics that you can get from excavation missions in different planets and void fissures vary from level 5 missions to level whatever-the-♥♥♥♥ and you can do them within your first hours, therefore getting items that you can immediatly sell to other players and start building your own economy.
THIS IS TRUE F2P, I♥♥♥♥♥♥YOU NOT.
The last thing I have to say is that the "design philosophy" behind the game doesn't try to make you feel weak by throwing giant bullet sponges at you, but try to make you feel hella ♥♥♥♥ing powerful by making you able to destroy enemies with (not-that-much-but-still-)over-the-top abilities and weapons, but punishes you with a huge shotgun blast or missile to the ear if you don't pay attention, almost immediatly downing you depending on the level of the enemy.
I'd go on for a while but I'll let you enjoy this ♥♥♥♥ing awesome game. It's one of the best online games I've ever played and I'm no casual scrub, I've played MANY.
PS: The story is ♥♥♥♥ing AWESOME, but you don't start it until you get to Neptune, so go hard on those junctions with the hype meter all the way up, mf.

Type of Game:
Vertical Endless Runner (there really isn’t an appropriate genre for this game)

The Good:
- An excellent time waster that will keep you engaged throughout your 5 – 6 hour playthrough
- Unlocks and in game purchases (no IAPs here) keep you coming back to play just “one more game”
- The challenge system especially keeps you motivated as it constantly adds a new “quests” for the player to complete for in game gold (ex: reach a certain height without falling or blow up ‘x’ amount of monsters with a bomb)
- Colorful and vibrant character/monster designs are welcome and keep the game feeling playful
- Fast gameplay sessions make it an excellent game to load up when you just want a quick game fix
- Numerous enemy types make for a nice variety of game strategy as they are introduced deliberately at appropriate intervals of progression
- Playing with a gamepad is intuitive and responsive, but not the best way to play the game (see below)
The Bad:
- Being a fan of the free flash version I was expecting the game to feature mouse controls, which were the best way to play the game. Unfortunately, at the time of this writing mouse controls are not part of the game
- The overall length of the main game is only about 4-5 hours, which  is quite short. While it features an endless mode, I never felt compelled to jump into that due to the lack of an end goal

I've used Stockfish before buying this, but I needed a complete pro software package with an existing pro opening book, a powerful database and functions to make custom opening books. After watching a video on how to use Fritz 15 to make a book, I decided to buy it and add the Stockfish engine to it. I made a pro book in 2 full days of heavy processing of 100,000s of games, thanks to the powerful Fritz database functions. Not bad considering I can learn from it for months or years to come. And I can develop my opening book further anytime. This is what serious players sometimes do, not for playing just friends but rather, also for competing on a much higher level. I can also make opening books on individual opening lines, like the Sicilian Dragon for example. Not just complete repertoires. You can change the weights of moves in the opening books as well, so if you find a drawish line, you might want the computer to avoid those lines, unless you're preparing to play a draw-master.
And then after achieving what I wanted to do with Fritz 15 so far, I noticed, the opening book plays reverse openings (it will treat 1.e3 e5 2.e4 as a reverse 1.e4 e5 - just a simple example) and it correctly uses ALL the same stats for each and every reverse move. This is especially important when white loses a tempi mid or late opening.
And then I noticed, the built-in training functions are way better than previous versions (I used to regularly use Fritz years ago). By default, often Fritz let me know after making a move what its main threat is. I turned this feature off since I already train to see these immediate threats, without hints. (It's long term threats that are difficult to see.)
And then, to my surprise, Fritz drew the first game it played against Stockfish on my machine. Stockfish won the overall match, but Fritz is a good alt engine if you want to try a different style player. But like I said, Fritz 15 is more than an engine, it's a complete package.
To a beginner, this makes no difference right away, but if you're serious about Chess, this program is great for years of high level training and practice. Fritz will even adjust to your level of play in Friend mode if you choose, which I'd recommend playing often, but try the hardest level at least sometimes to get a better idea of top level play. Note, there is no fast way of mastering Chess, it takes time, and this program is one of great value for learning to play really tight, if used right.
The GUI is a bit complicated, but not nearly as complicated as Chess, so if you play Chess well, you can get used to the GUI. I had an easier GUI for engines, but it didn't have all the functions I was looking for. There are some things I don't like but you get used to it. When I press New Game, I also seem to have to press Levels to play the AI. However, when analyzing, I simply press New Game and don't have to stop the engine from playing, so I can analyze my tournament games or set up a position to search for in the database without interruption.
If you prefer Stockfish or another engine, you probably still need a GUI and an opening book! The Fritz opening book is much more powerful and accurate for strength of moves, than any free opening book I've seen out there. There's a free opening book based on millions of games, but it has many weak variations in it (noticeable to someone doing proper opening study).
I'm using a quad core with 8 GB RAM, and have no problems with the GUI. On a slower computer, it might seem to freeze, but it's probably running the CPU at nearly 100%, which is normal, unless you're playing Friend mode or reducing the number of cores like I often do. I can run Fritz 15 on 2 cores and still have 2 cores for Windows and other apps, and my fan doesn't even turn on as the CPU can easily handle it no problem without overheating. With 4 cores running Fritz, the game makes maximum use of the full computing power available, if preparing a tournament opening line or maximizing the moves per second.
Note to serious players: you can also add endgame tablebases to Fritz 15, which will play any position within its base perfectly. There are up to 7-piece tablebases, not sure if 7 works, but up to 6-pieces should work perfectly. I've had 6pcs years ago. Haven't tried it in Fritz 15 yet. Great for analyzing tournament games, or boosting your computer's elo.
So, no I don't use the Fritz 15 engine often, but I use the Fritz opening book, GUI, database and opening book creation functions (there are easy videos on how to do this). For that alone, it's worth the price. Haven't tried online features yet, as I'm busy preparing openings and sometimes playing complete games against the AI to ready myself for the city championship.
I could've bought a previous version of Fritz, but I wanted the up-to-date Fritz 15 opening book, and to use newer functions.
It's too bad many are quick to judge the value here. If you simply want beautiful graphics and a little fun, there are other programs out there, some free, but you might learn bad moves from those programs and you might even have chessmaster friends who can beat that software. For a tournament Chess player or a beginner who wants to master the game, Fritz is well worth the money.
Sometimes one must research before investing money, ...and your precious time! Chess is not an easy game.
If you play Chess for 1000s of hours, why not spend a few 100 hours learning, experimenting and training properly? Or if you don't have much time for Chess but would like to learn fast, use Fritz 15 to see where the threats are, and correct blunders, etc. Chess is a great way to keep the mind sharp and to get an example of how incredible AI can be!! Man vs Machine, anyone?
I spent an hour to write this review. In business, I can charge as much as I paid for this software for an hour's work, but after seeing so many negative reviews I had to write this, for the community! Fritz 15, saved me many hours developing my opening book so far, for tournament level play. And when I'm unsure about the opening book I created I can use the Fritz 15 opening book, database or analysis features to test each move.
Very highly recommended!!

Amazing presentation and much more streamlined compared to the predecessor. But as comfortable as the simplification is, the complexity of the first game, including its story, feels much deeper and more stimulating.
The cutscenes are incredible. Even the talking parts are visually interesting. There are a lot of interesting set pieces but also a lot of underdesigned levels. It's dull to take cover, shoot everything that moves, advance and repeat. Maybe the level designers wanted you to be more aggressive and fight at the front. But the game is over when Shepard falls. So it's basically high risk but no reward. Your team mates can't use medigel on you. They should be a little more intelligent to back you up when you are playing dangerous. Or better yet there should be an option how they should behave. Like using techs and biotics nonstop.
The story is kind of bareboned but there is nothing wrong with a simple premise per se. The design and the writing of the characters make them memorable but everyone feels rather isolated. You get a feel for the individual, but they do not play off each other. A few don't get along, which also doesn't help to consider everyone a team. I think the main threat is not established well enough. Or should I say: Not early enough... visually. Words don't cut it. You need to witness the devastation first-hand a lot sooner for better emotional throughline. And I didn't believe for a second this was a "suicide mission". You should be on the clock to get a better grasp of what's at stake. No one comments on your leadership when you take your sweet time traveling around.
If compared to Mass Effect 1 a lot of elements are... I wouldn't say missing but abscent from the sequel. Most notably regarding the equipment. There is no need to prepare because the micro-management has been significantly reduced. You have to collect ammunition but there is way less items to gather. No omni-tools, no omni-gel, no armour or patches. As a result of that you cannot sell stuff, which means money is rather tight. On the other hand it makes more sense that you level up after a mission.
You can still explore the galaxy and visit planets that aren't critical to the main mission. It's awesome that you can read about chemical and physical properties of planets and also that you can fly around instead of selecting everything from a menu. But you cannot drive around on the surface because there is no vehicle. All areas including the cities look and feel smaller in size - especially the Citadel. On the other hand the copypasta from the first game is gone. Could it be that there are fewer quests? Well, it's not like there is not enough content.
The structure is a little repetetive and predictable. You recruit all new team members, help them sort out a personal problem to gain their loyalty and then embark on the main mission. Inbetween you scan some planets and collect resources. I know these loops are inherent to game design but they are very transparent in this case. It consists literally of the sum of its parts.
I find the emotional resonance from the narrative rather lacking. It is too cold. This can be tracked back to weak direction. It should be a big deal to meet your old team members again. A little sentimentality is called for here. Kaidan/Ashley and especially Liara are a huge disappointment in my opinion. I found myself not caring all that much what's going on in particular missions and wanted to go back to the shooting - which is untypical for a script kiddie like me.
The game is very easy (I played on normal) so that you don't have to think or pay attention. You do not have to understand the mission objectives or what's at stake to follow it through. If you wanna be a paragon, you pick the upper dialogue choice. If renegade the lower. No exceptions. Reading the option itself is negligible. You can equip whatever to everyone and will be fine, which feels inconsequential and that's a problem.
They neglected to provide gamepad support, which I can't understand since it was developed for the XBox. You have to install a mod to have it reinstated. With that it is perfect to play and feels wonderful.
There are a couple of graphical glitches that make characters jump around in the frame. No disaster, really, just funny and a bit immersion breaking. Somehow I got stuck on a ledge twice in different places where I couldn't get off, only after I reloaded the checkpoint. And then there was this one time Shepard's model was facing in the opposite direction. Opening the menu fixed it. Also some lines are repeated twice in a row, which is kinda funny. Maybe it's due to my low cpu speed. Or it's the aforementioned mod, I don't know. The game is very stable otherwise.
The german localisation is top-notch but there are some issues. Sometimes the subtitle has problems with punctuation and shows blank symbols instead of commas. And the spoken word differs from the captions in a few places - sometimes drastically.
Bottom line, it's a fun game but not so much an RPG anymore. It is dumbed down and therefore more accessible, which means easier to play and to like. But it doesn't challenge your wits nor your heart.

'Submerged' takes you on a mysterious journey into a submerged city on a quest to save your brothers life. While you search for supplies to heal your brother you also reveal your past and the story of the city.
The main aim in this game is to find collectibles that are scattered all over the city. Most of the time you have to climb the ruins on your search for supplies. Climbing feels a little like in 'Tomb Raider' or 'Assassins Creed' and there's not much more to do than search, climb and collect. Some players think this concept is too simple to recommend this game but I loved it. It's true, it's simple and very short. But the atmosphere of this sunken world is amazing and I enjoyed every minute of 'Submerged'.
Pros:
- nice graphics
- good music
- very good, realistic sound effects
- great atmosphere
- open word
- changing weather that feels very realistic, watch the thunderstorms
- day and night cycle
- you can't die
- mild horror elements
- mysterious
- exceptional
- turns buildings into puzzles
- very good camera control
- possibility to continue exploring the city after finishing the main story
- whales
- post card option for extra beautiful screenshots
- I took more than 200 screenshots in 7 hours
Cons:
- climbing gets a little repetitive but since the story is not too long I think it's OK
- a little too simple
- short
'Submerged' is probably not a game for everybody but if you're looking for something peaceful, relaxing and simply want to experience the mood of this amazing world don't hesitate and give this game a try. 'Submerged' definitely deserves a recommendation if on sale.

Up front, I have to say that this game isn't for everybody. Those looking for action, deep stories, or challenging gameplay should look elsewhere. The gameplay is extremely simple, not a word of english is spoken in-game, and it doesn't have any enemies or even a fail state of any sort. It's impossible to "lose" in any way in this game.
All that being said, I thoroughly enjoyed every moment I spent with this game, short though it may have been. This game is all about ATMOSPHERE, and it has an incredible one. The game managed to find a unique and visually striking post-apocalyptic setting, and populated it with beautiful monuments and awe-inspiring wildlife. The score alone is worth the price of admission, consisting of a number of beautiful and haunting piano pieces which excellently set the tone of the game.
It's not very long, and I would call it mercifully so as there simply isn't much to do in-game. There are landmarks and wildlife to hunt down, as well as one-note boat upgrades and a bunch of hidden secrets, each of which reveals a panel of story which collectively add up to explain what happened to create this lush yet haunting world. The meat of the gameplay consists of 10 emergency macguffin boxes you must track down to aid your ailing brother. Each of the boxes sits at the top of a large building you must climb, navigating a maze-like series of branching paths and attempting to track down secrets along the way. Ultimately, these climbing sections are simple, and there are no puzzles or challenges to be found.
Voice acted lines ingame are rare and consist of a fictional language. The entirety of the story of this game (other than your "quest" objectives) is conveyed via comic-like panels containing pictograms of scenes and events. It's confusing at first, but becomes crystal clear as more blanks are filled in. The backstory of the main characters is heartbreaking even though it's basically conveyed through stick figures.
First and foremost, this is an exploration game. It's never more fun than when you are just driving around in your boat, looking for new landmarks and creatures to add to your journal. This could be a perfect game for the non-gamer in your life who couldn't handle a challenging game but still wants an engaging experience. Some could call it boring, and I couldn't really argue with them, but I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. I got it on sale for $5. I don't know if I would pay more than that, considering how short it is, but it is definitely worth checking out. You might even feel a feeling or two.

I bought this after the 1.6 patch came out, and it's FANTASTIC. It feel very much like a Dungeon Keeper 3 game.
Pros:
• Same DK mechanics you know and love
• Much better graphics (I don't have to play DK2 anymore)
• You now drop prioners into crypts to turn them into undead
• some objects have multiple modes -- for example, you can torture to turn into a ghost or convert
• Very stable. I haven't crashed once in over 8 hours of play.
• Logical and fun changes to make the game feel fresh (like the Necromancer!)
• The Chunder is really funny -- his entire head is a hammer, which he uses to construct traps.
• The voice!
As I said, the game very much feels like "Dungeon Keeper 3", which is a good thing. This game brings out all the good mechanics and gameplay of DK2, but adds a few extra layers, like spell unlocking (you can now choose).  I am especially happy that I don't have to send units topside -- the entire game takes place underground in the dungeon.
That being said, I do have some minor gripes:
Cons:
• Everyone is so grey. I would have liked more color to differentiate the units -- but this is a problem with the previous DK series too
• The campaign starts a little slow for DK vet like me, but it's actually good for new players that aren't familiar with the series.
Any fan of DK or DUNGEONS should give this game a go. It always gives me goosebumps when I hear the narrater say "IT'S PAYDAY!"

Like many of the other negative reviews on Steam, I want to preface my review by saying that I loved Lugaru, and think Overgrowth - even as it is now - is fun, and I hope it'll be a finished product one day.
That being said, the only question Steam reviews should answer is: do you recommend buying the game? The thing is, I really don't.
I bought Overgrowth years ago, and even though a lot of work has been put into it since, it's very much the same game I played back then. It looks better, has more character models, better UI, all that good stuff.
it still doesn't have any substance. It's not a sequel to Lugaru, it's a sandbox tech demo, where you can play around with the Overgrowth engine. And to be fair, the Steam store description and Early Access information both make this very clear.
I have no doubt that if Overgrowth ever gets finished it'll be worth the $30€ price tag. But right now, I wouldn't recommend buying it. People interested in Overgrowth for what it is currently will  buy it regardless of my recommendation, but I think people looking for a game, should definitely wait, unless they're willing to think of the purchase as a pre-order with an undefined release date.
Things that have happened while Overgrowth has been in development: Barack Obama get's elected president of the United States, Apple debuted the iPad, the first solar-sail tech demonstration is produced, Osama bin Laden is killed, Japan suffers the effects of a massive earthquake and a tsunami, the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform exploded in the Gulf of Mexico causing the worst marine enviromental disaster in US history, 3d printers and scanners enter the consumer market, mouse genome is fully sequenced, world population breaks the 7 billion mark, usb 3.0 is introduced, 22nm chips begin mass production, Curiosity is launched and lands on mars, I got married, got a job, lost the job, moved houses four times and learned to juggle.
Overgrowth is the indie Daikatana. Except unlike Daikatana, Overgrowth when finished will be awesome, and not the most mediocre entry in its genre.

Agatha Christie - The ABC Murders
Lets get this out of the way first, this game is around 5-8 hours in length for a single play though and that depends on how fast you are at figuring out the puzzles. The puzzles and interrogations are the hardest parts in this game and offer real challenge to the player. Puzzles range from opening boxes to solving chinese word problems.
Interrogations offer the biggest challenge to someone who isn't following along with the story and how the various characters react, as you have one and only one chance to ask or accuse. If you mess up a question, the story will move on and you will not have another chance.
Clues are handled differently, as you as Poirot says "Put those little grey cells to work" has you actually take conversations and clues to prove certain things. Ranging from the pych make up of the killer to why this young lady left her possessions behind.
Voice Acting is a large part of adventure games and ABC Murders gets a talented actor for Poirot keeps the bar high. The various other people you meet are hit or miss, with the hotel manager as the low for me.
Overall: I enjoyed the ABC Murders though it was a bit short. If you enjoy murder mysteries or adventure games you should buy this.

I highly recommend this game. For the review I just want to touch on some points I disagree with other reviewers on.
Some people say the controls on this game are clunky but I tend to disagree. The skating mechanics reward players when they choose smart lines throughout the environments and when these lines are executed perfectly. If you fail to hit a grind on a rail you were going for, or missed a wall ride, you'll have to regain your momentum. But this game isn't like, say, Assassins Creed, where you can press one button and seamlessly bust moves over your environment with little to no input from the player. Jet Set Radio actually requires skill to maintain maximum mobility which makes it a deeper experience.
The graffitti mechanics where you have to follow arrow directions to spray paints objects works well, even with a keyboard once you get the hang of it. It adds an elements of strategy in each level where you have to determine if it's safe to spray certain places when you're being chased by the cops or assassins.
This is all I wanted to touch on since I figure other reviews have fleshed out all of the other features of this game. 10/10 for me.
Hasn't aged well, but worth a try, wait for a 75% off or better sale, since age has already taken it's full toll, lol.

This is a really good game, on the premise that you prefer long, involved, in-depth and open type gameplay.

BIGGEST FACTORS describing this game -
OLD STYLE MMO - the long, involved, open world, tons of players, tons of items and crafting type game.
REAL TIME FPS COMBAT - Usually antagonistic to the above, but this game ACTUALLY HAS REAL TIME COMBAT!!
This is one of the few games out there that actually merge a real open-world MMO with real-time shooting and hand-to-hand combat.
This is very rare and what makes this game so overlooked and underrated.
BIGGEST DOWNSIDE TO GAME - The Majority of Players overlook the incredible teamwork mechanics and end up just running solo as 'shooter' type (FPS) classes.
When you see how rich and deep they made the combat and team-work mechanics it becomes an absolute shame so few players take the time to actually team up to fight and adventure together.
This is excarcebated by the quick leveling which allows solo style gameplay to progress too far in the game.
General notes -
It is - not - for those wanting a quick-fix or something flashy and giving quick gratification.
All it's 'good' things are exactly what a different type of player would find as 'bad'
- Dark, almost 'dreary' atmosphere means some will find it too dark and depressing, but others will enjoy the nitty-gritty feel and realistiic ambiance.
- long involved crafting - can be a pain due to the amount of quests you need to do to get recipes etc, but that's what makes it enjoyable for those who like to have a big world to explore
- A very different type of story-line - gets you involved in something that's actually quite realistic (there is no fiction in this game, all teh technology exists etc), but others might not 'get' it and not see the point
- An actual open world - there's so much to do you can easily outlevel your zone, you have a lot of places to explore and quests to do, others that are used to XBox games will find it a bit daunting and aimless.
- Huge player base, I played a few months ago and there were many guilds (outfits, whatever they're called) and with all the different types of classes you have lots of game-style options.
A very good game, definitely over-loked and under-rated (as other reviewers mentioned), just as long as you realize it's long and involved, don't expect quick-fixes or 'leet' type gameplay.
Basically - this MMO if actually really good because it fits the 'old-style' MMO genre, an actual open world with lots of team-play mechanics.  If you play it well you'll get one of the most incredible values out of any game you can get.
Downsides were as mentioned - the dark atmosphere can actually get depressing if you play it too long (lol), and, the #1 reason I didn't stick around after a while was because the mechanics are actually - Fantastic - in this game, BUT, 99% of players just end up 'going solo Gun-man' style (becoming lone FPS type players, instead of working synergistically as a team with all the amazing classes available in the game).
Great game, - Old style MMO experience, with the 'New' style FPS real-time combat mechanics.

A forgotten gem from the Dreamcast era, now back and polished with HD graphics!
Jet Set Radio was a truly stylish and unique game for its time (in fact it still is today, save for its sequel) and I have to say that while its in-game mechanics, the freedom it gives you and its length are kind of lacking for today's standards, it still remains a great and fun game (though it can get a bit annoying at times, for difficulty related reasons)!
The graphics and backgrounds were already good, but with the HD upgrade they are now great, full of vivid colors and vitality, it is not by sheer luck that Cel Shaded graphics were popularized by this game.
The soundtrack is equally awesome, filled with many kinds of music genres, mostly of japanese and american provenience and pretty much helps set the tone and atmosphere of the game.
The story isn't much, it plays mostly like a parody movie, but for a game like this it isn't expected to, instead, it is filled with many humorous and witty lines, spoken from the mouth of DJ Professor K.
All in all, despite the years on its back, this is still a very fun one-of-a-kind game and as such I urge all of you to try it sometime. It already is cheap and on sales it's even cheaper!
Hopefully Sega will someday remember and decide to give us an HD port of the game's sequel, Jet Set Radio Future, originally available on the first Xbox, since I had found that to be bigger in everything (graphics, soundtrack and open world) and not that much dated compared to today's games!
The Dreamcast era, my favorite gaming era, is sadly over, but it's thanks to HD Ports like this that it continues to live... and with the now announced revival of Shenmue 3 (google it if you don't know what it is, we are talking about my absolute favorite games ever) all I can say is... long live childhood years!

Multiple times i have had to shut down and restart the game completely because the "Stun" move simply stops working. It will be fully charged and ready to go and it just won't work. Simple as that. Lost many long sessions because of this bug.
And the game does a poor job at explaining its own gameplay mechanics (see below)
-Game tells you that you will recieve an additional unit to defend the tower if you upgrade the barracks to the max. But they fail to inform you if that unit is effected by levels, buffers, powerups and they also fail to tell you what type of unit and if that unit can score critical hits or not. Things like this are important to know in strategy games.
-Game allows you to upgrade your player speed and health but fails to inform you if those upgrades carry over to the other gametypes like survival and escape.
-Game lists a "Healer" but feels no need to tell you that the healer sacrifices her OWN health to give you more.
-Towards the end of the game enemies leave a random skull and crossbones stake in the ground and i have no idea what they are. The game does not tell you.
-One perk says "Keep shops open longer, increase drop rate by 50%" which costs 2000 gold, while another perks with a golden axe says "Double your gold drop rate and look good while doing it". Well i purchased the 2000 gold perk and enemies who dropped 13gold before still drop 13 gold now. So obviously that perk is only referring to musical tune drops which would have been nice to know before i spent 2000 gold.
-Game allows you to upgrade your units but fails to explain why characters still "Level up" after killing enemies. Why are my maxxed out units still leveling up?
-Game tells you units can score critical hits at higher levels but fail to inform you what chance the unit has to score a critical chance or how much more damage a critical hit does.
-Game shows a speed boost buffer but doesn't feel the need to inform you that the speed buffer also increases your units rate of fire as well as movement speed. These things would have been nice to know beforehand.
-Game tells you that the bards rate of musical notes increase while idle, but do not inform you how much more. Same goes for units like the mechanic which build turrets after standing idle for a period of time, they don't tell you how long it takes standing still before he builds a turret and they do not tell you how much damage the turret does or if the turret can score critical hits or not.
-Game does not have a counter to tell you how many active units you have out on the battlefield at once, In the early stage of the game it is easy to count but good luck when you are able to have 9 at once and you have maxxed out "Body spray". Yeah good luck counting 9 individual units all twirling/spinning/sprinting around with thousands of rocks/missiles coming at you.
It just seems silly to fail to explain simple gameplay mechanics in a game where strategy is key. A small strategical difference can mean the difference between victory or defeat. And the fact that this company does not even feel the need to explain to you what is happening on the battlefield in complete detail is extremely ignorant.
And the overall gameplay setup of the game is just poor. Instead of perks being a bonus to give you an edge over your opponent, its mandatory pre-requisite required to proceed through the campaign. The game is purposely setup to force the player to grind for experience/gold. For example, in order to get past stage2, you need about two hours worth of gold farming to upgrade your characters. Even if you do everything properly in terms of strategy, you simply will not do enough DPS to stop the kamikaze bomber before he reaches your base.
And ironically, for a game that is called "Bardbarian" and is centered around guitar shredding and musical notes. It only has one mediocre background tune for all three game types.

What do I say? I just got lucky, picked up the software for 18$ instead of the 60$.
While there are decent free available alternatives for most of the features Fritz provides, its still an all-in-one solution for any Amateur to Candidate level chess player.
The biggest mistake people here on Steam make is in thinking that this is a fancy chess game, IT ISN'T.
Think of it as an educational tool which helps you learn, improve, train and play against any engine of your choice.
Also comes with a 6 month premium subscription for Chessbase which is also pretty cool.
For my Indian friends, Fritz15 is on an INSANE price just north of 18$ do pick it up if you want to have some money to spare and want to learn and improve in this amazing game.
Only CONS that I see are:
-The software is still slightly buggy since its pretty recent, and now that I have it for around 18$, 60$ for the rest feels a little overpriced when you can acquire Fritz14 for much cheaper and 90% of it is the same. IF you have good money to spare, go for Fritz15, otherwise go for Fritz14.
-The 3D pieces are pretty buggy and VERY tasking on the CPU.But I can easily live without them and use 2D pieces (which they have a huge collection of).
-There are many free alternatives for 'basic chess stuff' like playing against people/computers, analyzing/watching games, annotating ,maintaining an opening repertoire/game databases like

etc.

Nominated for the "Choices Matter" Award.  The choices you make in this game have some minor effect on the gameplay and story of Mass Effect 3.  Hard to imagine this game is almost 8 years old at the time of this review.  Great graphics that still hold up after all these years, some of Bioware's best voice acting and casting, extremely well written teammates you actually give a damn about.  Combat is intense, exciting, and responsive, arguably the best in the series, since Mass Effect 3 made the mistake of having spacebar be assigned to sprint, take cover, vault cover all at once, which led to some frustrations in that game.   DLC that is largely interesting and worth the cost, with the exception of the Hammerhead DLC missions.  Those add nothing to the game overall, and are completely forgettable, not worth the time and energy, and doesn't get mentioned in ME3.  Other than that, the DLC is amazing.  Lair of the Shadow Broker, while was given a notoriously poor review by PC Gamer, story wise was still the best storyline in the franchise.  Overlord was praised by some for its sensitive depiction of autism, though I personally felt it was a bit disproportionately difficult compared to the other DLC and main story.
In short, there's a reason this game has been tagged as "Overwhelmingly Positive" in review scores.  The graphics and sound are amazing, the combat is engaging, the characters are iconic, the voice acting is legendary, and the ending level is praised as one of the greatest final levels in a video game, of all time.  A great deal at full price, and is definitely worth it when it's on special.  Now if you'll excuse me, I should go.

An extremely mellow short film of a game, Submerged is by no means a bad game, but it outstays its welcome and completely fails to justify its $20 pricetag.
While I did purchase it for sale at $5, which I think is a significantly more reasonable asking price for what it is, it doesn't change the fact that the game is about 4-5 hours long and has enough story for maybe half that. Its pictographic record of what happened to the city and what led you there is fairly redundant, which I suspect was so you could piece together a reasonably clear picture without going out of your way to collect all the secrets, but it's most apparent that the game doesn't have that much to say when halfway through your flashbacks between missions change from an explanation of the past to literally just recapping the opening cutscene and the game itself.
Gameplay-wise, Submerged is just another Ubisoft-style sandbox hidden behind a mellow, mysterious atmosphere that brings to mind Shadow of the Colossus if you took out all the fights with colossi. Find a waypoint, climb to the waypoint, repeat until win. Calling the climbing mechanics parkour would be inaccurate to say the least - there's no skill challenge involved, no possibility of failure and no room for intuitive thinking. You can only climb on specific sorts of ledges, even when there are easy shortcuts clearly within the realm of your character's physical abilities.
All in all it works, especially since the main draw of the game is the relaxed atmosphere, but it's just not enough to justify its purchase or the time needed to play through it.

Of all the games I have played throughout the years, none have compared to Crusader Kings II. Not a single playthrough in the 700+ hours I have spent in-game has been the same as a previous one. Former empires crumbling early due to weak leaders, small duchies becoming kingdoms through an early conquest. Many things change from one game to the next. When I first played the game, I had a very difficult time understanding all the mechanics and how to figure out many of the details that lie within the game. It's a very complex game to be sure but once you unravel it all, it's more than worth the effort it takes to learn the game!
I would suggest watching a few tutorial videos on youtube to learn the game mechanics. While outdated, they explain a lot of the concepts. Eviscerator03 helped me a lot in particular. I followed him in his campaign while doing the same one of my own to learn. Also, doing achievement runs seemed to help as well. While unlocking a whole bunch of them, I learned a lot more about the mechanics and how to accomplish goals through a different course than I would have before.
Don't wait! Buy Crusader Kings II now and create a dynasty to stand through the ages!

This is a really good game, on the premise that you prefer long, involved, in-depth and open type gameplay.

BIGGEST FACTORS describing this game -
OLD STYLE MMO - the long, involved, open world, tons of players, tons of items and crafting type game.
REAL TIME FPS COMBAT - Usually antagonistic to the above, but this game ACTUALLY HAS REAL TIME COMBAT!!
This is one of the few games out there that actually merge a real open-world MMO with real-time shooting and hand-to-hand combat.
This is very rare and what makes this game so overlooked and underrated.
BIGGEST DOWNSIDE TO GAME - The Majority of Players overlook the incredible teamwork mechanics and end up just running solo as 'shooter' type (FPS) classes.
When you see how rich and deep they made the combat and team-work mechanics it becomes an absolute shame so few players take the time to actually team up to fight and adventure together.
This is excarcebated by the quick leveling which allows solo style gameplay to progress too far in the game.
General notes -
It is - not - for those wanting a quick-fix or something flashy and giving quick gratification.
All it's 'good' things are exactly what a different type of player would find as 'bad'
- Dark, almost 'dreary' atmosphere means some will find it too dark and depressing, but others will enjoy the nitty-gritty feel and realistiic ambiance.
- long involved crafting - can be a pain due to the amount of quests you need to do to get recipes etc, but that's what makes it enjoyable for those who like to have a big world to explore
- A very different type of story-line - gets you involved in something that's actually quite realistic (there is no fiction in this game, all teh technology exists etc), but others might not 'get' it and not see the point
- An actual open world - there's so much to do you can easily outlevel your zone, you have a lot of places to explore and quests to do, others that are used to XBox games will find it a bit daunting and aimless.
- Huge player base, I played a few months ago and there were many guilds (outfits, whatever they're called) and with all the different types of classes you have lots of game-style options.
A very good game, definitely over-loked and under-rated (as other reviewers mentioned), just as long as you realize it's long and involved, don't expect quick-fixes or 'leet' type gameplay.
Basically - this MMO if actually really good because it fits the 'old-style' MMO genre, an actual open world with lots of team-play mechanics.  If you play it well you'll get one of the most incredible values out of any game you can get.
Downsides were as mentioned - the dark atmosphere can actually get depressing if you play it too long (lol), and, the #1 reason I didn't stick around after a while was because the mechanics are actually - Fantastic - in this game, BUT, 99% of players just end up 'going solo Gun-man' style (becoming lone FPS type players, instead of working synergistically as a team with all the amazing classes available in the game).
Great game, - Old style MMO experience, with the 'New' style FPS real-time combat mechanics.

I love Agatha Christie's book. Her writing is sharp, her characters are full of color and personality and her murder mysteries are masterpieces.  She is the mama of modern murder mysteries. Pros:
- Great story
- Superb voice acting (esp the rendition of Poirot) and music
- Innovative graphics - sort of cell shading
Cons:
- Frantic clicking to solve mysteries
- Repetitive puzzles which do not help in detective work
- Slow in certain areas
While I liked the feel of the game and the way they translated the story to a PC game, the puzzles you have in the game rapidly turn repetitive. The best feature in the game is the "grey cells" portion where you help Poirot make a deduction out of the observations made in the game.  I was actually looking for this everytime.  And the music is superb.
Overall, Buy this game if it is on sale. Decent game to pass the afternoon.

I love mystery games and like Agatha Christie, so I am sorry not to be able to recommend this. It had some good points, but overall was a disappointment to the genre.
Pros:
* Reasonably good art, at its best points charming.
* Voice acting is good enough to carry the story.
* Automatic assessments of how people are feeling based on body language as you interrogate/interview them.
* Adaptive interview techniques: as you assess someone's character and what they respond to, you can change your line of questioning. (The point system gives you feedback by awarding you points for the perfect response, though because it's a varying number of points, it's hard to know if you chose the best one or just a not-terrible option.)
* It's fun to get points for checking the mirror every chance you get and grooming your mustache. It adds to the conceited, easy to dislike character that is classic Poirot.
Cons:
* Railroaded experience (no pun intended.) At first you are chasing the ABC killer; you know who has committed these murders and why, and are still forced to investigate a lot of other suspects before concluding "Yes, it's that same killer I was obviously chasing!" Then when a forced twist comes, you are similarly walked through the rest of the game.
* Unless I was insanely lucky or something, Steam achievements really are handed out for next to nothing. There are ten or so for finishing a section, in a game I finished in about six hours. That's only a fraction but is representative of the 50 to be had.
* As you question someone, it is sometimes obvious what tactic to take with them, but you still get the dialogue options wrong because the summary of what you want to say is misleading. E.g., what may seem like a reasonable question makes them angry because you unexpectedly say it in an insulting way.
* Observations of a suspect or scene have nothing to do with your own perceptiveness. The reticule changes from white to green as you zero in on whatever the designers wanted you to notice.
* A conclusion system modeled after the Sherlock Holmes games, but too flawed to be interesting. If you insert the right clues into the open spaces (which is sometimes frustrating, if you don't know what conclusion Poirot is trying to draw), it automatically tells you the meaning. For example, "This suspect is innocent." You don't have to use your own powers of judgment.
* Repetitive mini-games involving manipulating objects. Apparently, every criminal in this world has a similar lockbox that involves sliding bits of wood and copying patterns from elsewhere in the room.
* The final conclusion of the one crime you're investigating throughout the game is very unsatisfying. The motives are boring, the proof of guilt is unconvincing, the assumptions behind the guilty party are logically flawed in some very obvious ways, and at last only a Perry Mason-style blurted confession proves that Poirot got it right. I personally formed a much more interesting theory to implicate someone else, a suspect that was never even seriously questioned.
So, I did get an interesting six hours out of following Poirot around. But the most enjoyable part of the game was yelling at our hero for stumbling around wasting time on silly leads, which isn't the basis of a good detective game.

Who this game may appeal to –
-New P&C gamers
-Agatha Christie fans or those who love a good story
-HOG gamers who like puzzles as the puzzles here are just a bit harder than most HOGs (note this isn't a HOG like some past Christie games were).
-People who find Nancy Drew and Sherlock Holmes games too hard or need a good bit of help with them.
Those who are seasoned P&C gamers who are expecting the same length and complexities as the cheaper priced ($20) new Nancy Drew games may be disappointed which is why I am only recommending it if you can get it at half price.  But then I always found Agatha Christie games to be easier than ND and SH games (although this is a completely different style as to the other AC adventure games).  Trying to be thorough going for max points and working out achievements, first gameplay was 6-7hrs, with no hints.
The gameplay is easy as there are objectives that are scored out so you know when you have done everything in an area and can move on to the next objective.  The hotspots for areas in scenes are generous so it’s hard to miss anything and there are optional hints if needed (have no idea how they work or if you can skip puzzles with them.)
At most there are two areas at a time for you to explore so you can’t get lost and thankfully there is not a lot of inventory items ever in the game so no trying to combine a lot of things or trying items on every hotspot you come across.  Gameplay is very linear.
The puzzles are easy and a couple do get annoying with the repetitiveness of them, but some will take you a while not because they are fundamentally hard but the execution of some of them is fiddly and a couple makes you think they will be harder than they actually are.  If you hate all puzzles/minigames then this game isn’t for you as I’d class this as a puzzle/adventure.
The observations of people you can’t get wrong and in scenes it tells you how many clues there are to find so that’s easy as well.  Where it gets not relaxing is limited dialogue choices which can frustrate as sometimes you don’t want to pick either choice and trying the nice route first which Poirot does in the books doesn’t always yield you max points.
The questions for the deduction board later sometimes didn’t always gel with the facts you give to support it.  I am used to the more complex and better Sherlock Holmes deduction boards where the hardness is in trying to remember your facts and what goes with something but in this game it’s more the ambiguity of the questions sometimes.
I have read the book so I found the deductions and questions to be easier, if you haven’t read the book I could imagine you might find that side of the game to be harder but with limited choices re deduction board you will get it quickly.
The one thing I find ultra-annoying is that there is no manual save game system, which for me is a basic need especially with a game with points and achievements.  I kept wanting to retry conversations and try different things but I couldn’t.
I do appreciate that there are built in achievements, a timeline which helps you understand the story better at the end and points.
I sadly find P&C games to be rare so I devour ones I find and I will buy all the hopefully future Agatha Christie games there will be, not just because of this but also I am a huge Agatha Christie fan.  But for $24 I wished it was either longer, or more non-linear, have more areas to explore or more in-depth complexities of gameplay, maybe fewer but harder puzzles.
It was a good but not a great game and of course the plot and story was excellent, overall I did really enjoy it and there is replayability in trying to get all achievements.  I’d give it a 7/10.

It starts off being maybe a little overwhelming, but I quickly found my feet. Particularly if you follow the campaign, you get introduced to each new asset as things go along, which helps.

We learn nothing really about Oberon. The Heart of Gold campaign was more fun (for me anyway) because I knew Kasita and what she was interested in. But if you just want to hack your way into another Underlord's dungeon, that's available too.

True to the spirit of Agatha Christie, this game offers an enthralling tale of murder and mystery. You play as Hercule Poirot, the famed Belgium detective out to solve another crime with his trusted companion Mr. Hastings. The story is engaging and well paced and like Agatha Christie's novels, will keep you guessing till the very end of who is the A.B.C. Murderer.
Gameplay wise, the mechanics are serviceable. There is noticeable roughness to be found with all aspects of the game, yet it does not detract from the experience. The puzzles are rather easy to solve, though this is most likely intentional as to not disrupt the flow of the narrative (there is a mechanic within the game where it will solve the next step of the puzzle for you if you happen to get stuck if you so choose). The game does a good job of telling you whether or not you are done within a certain area, making sure you do not miss any vital information that would hinder progress further along in the game.
The controls are a bit rough (played with mouse and keyboard), but nothing too troublesome. This game is fully voice acted, though there are moments where it felt a bit off. That being said, I found the person who voiced Poirot in this game to well casted and considering the fact that he is the central character, that is what I believe to matter the most. The aesthetic is pleasing and the game's selection of music is well suited to the narrative.
All in all, even though it has a few faults, it is nothing too large that would prevent me from recommending this game. The price point may be a bit high for some, so unless you are a fan of Agatha Christie (like I am), I would advise to wait for a modest sale.

Agatha Christie – The ABC Murders:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Umm . . . My dear Monsieur Hastings. Here we go again, investigating intriguing murders - but you see, mon cher ami, Hercule Poirot knows how to use his “matiere grise” (grey matter) to resolve any murders. Let’s look at the clues mon ami… Shall we?
Agatha Christie – The ABC Murders is a point and click adventure game where you play the incredibly famous Belgian detective, Hercule Poirot. At the start of the story, you will investigate the death of an old lady tobacconist. With your exceptional flair, you will gather clues, talk to people and try to put together an answer to this crime. Then you will be able to reconstruct the crime from start to finish. Be assured, it will not end there, as you will be following the trail of the ABC criminal mastermind. You will travel through England via train to several destinations where the murders took place.
I really enjoyed the game play; not only are you looking for clues and talking to people but you are also observing them and trying to understand who they are or what they may hiding from the police. In terms of the puzzles, if you like point and click games like myself, you might find most of them average or even simple on some occasions.

The 3D graphics are great and the voice over is superb, mes chers amis. The controls are nice and easy to use, as you would expect for this type of game.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Great graphics
-	Superb voice over
-	Easy to play
-	Achievements & trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Puzzles are quite simple
If you like point and click adventure games, Agatha Christie - The ABC Murders is a must have.

I have played the Spellforce series from the beginning, and loved every installment. Until this one. The side quests are completely boring, mostly just "go back to the last area you cleared and find an item or two." The combat is easy but everything takes way too long to die. They probably expect you to skip the terrible side quests, so maybe I was stronger than I should have been.
The dialogue is terrible, and not because it's translated from German. The translation is fine. Every conversation just is way longer than it needs to be, packed with unneccessary dialogue, and delivered at a pace that would bore a sloth. I usually read the entire line of dialogue before they'd said two words of it, but with plot dialogues you can't skip lines, you can only skip the whole conversation. So you have to sit and listen to the sloooooowest talking dragons rehash plot points from previous games to which your character replies "I know. I was there" before they move on to new information. Or you can skip the whole thing and learn nothing. I feel like I'm being punished for caring about the lore. At least I get to look at close up shots of said dragons, which would look decent for a game from the early 2000's. To be fair to the dragons, though, the elves/humans/ghosts are just as bad.
The level design is terrible as well. In order, the levels are: a level from the last games, but ON FIRE! Then the laziest designed map in the history of games: a bunch of small islands that you teleport between so that they didn't have to try to create a flowing envronment. Then the most frustrating city ever, because it's very large and you move very slowly and the crappy fog of war doesn't update until you actually walk inside one of the dozens of buildings looking for the thing you need to move the plot along. Then a different level from the last game, again, but WITH DEMONS! That's where I stopped, due to it suddenly becoming unplayable.
Oh, yeah. It doesn't even work. The series has always been buggy, but it's never been unplayable for me before. Some examples of bugs: if a character is talking, and you go into a dialogue, your character starts what he was saying over. Which was really annoying during one puzzle in the second level where you have to use trial and error and keep initializing dialogue with some objects, and every time you fail they say the exact same lines. So Caine would start to talk, I'd interact with the item, he'd start over, I'd click the next item, he'd start over, etc etc etc. In the five minutes it took me to solve, I probably heard that first line about 100 times. Next, after completing a side quest involving 6 items, it didn't remove those items from my invenory. So I just put them on inventory page 10; not a big deal, but shoddy work. What finally broke the game for me was in the fourth level I had to go kill an NPC that was formerly neutral, and when it told me to go kill her it never set her to hostile. Reloaded my backup save and trudged through the tedious fghts and crappy dialogue and guess what: same bug. Unistalled.
So, I didn't finish the game. From what I played though, the "25+ hours of gameplay" would probably be about 5 in a game with better pacing. Slow movement, slow combat, slow dialogue. No new units added, poor map design, poor writing. I have been progressively more disappointed in each installment of Spellforce 2. I'm gonna reinstall the original Spellforce to cheer myself up.

You wake up in 2076 in a yurt in the middle of a steppe and cannot remember a thing. There is a broken mechanical girl in your room, and a huge, abandoned dome nearby.  You can roam the world freely, interact with objects and physics, read tons of documents that help you understand what happened (think Gone Home and The Vanishing of Ethan Carter).
There are a lot or Orwellian things going on here, there is also a mysterious virus called 'desperatoxin' and some strange, smoke-like cratures. Your task is to repair your companion, explore the dome and learn what happened to the world and human society.

However, that all changed when the updates attacked.*proceeds to stare at the DLC using peripherals* He whispers solemnly, “I’ll be seeing you in a minute”. I have played this game for the better part of two years and I have to say that I absolutely hate the direction of the updates placed upon this game. Even though you can opt for old versions of the game in beta, I feel as though the game has moved backwards at times.
My most recent issue with the game stems from some bull crap I got during a war I started with Norway in Scandinavia. I attack and completely decimated their army, I also managed to take their capital and 80% of their fiefs (got like 1/100 percent for it). Even so, the war percent dropped form 80% to 30% in a second for no reason, I wasn’t even attacked. Long story short, other countries attacked me after like 30 years of holding all their counties and I lost. The game has some serious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t to work out and I’m tired of sitting in a game for hours on end strategizing for it to all crumble away due to unexplainable ♥♥♥♥ery. I’ve seen a lot of crap in my days playing this game (Believe it) but boy does this♥♥♥♥♥♥takes the cake. Nothing close has ever happened to me like this before the recent updates (At least not at this scale). I even summoned 7500 troops using my massive prestige and I was still defeated out of some form of broken attrition.
Now for my biggest gripe about the game *Walks over to DLC and whispers in its ear* “Its’ time”. Holy crap this game has more DLC then fricking Total war games. I bought the vanilla version of this game on sale for what I though was a reasonable price. However, shortly after I bought it, they released a “complete” edition of the game which I thought was all of the DLC. WRONG! I’ve never been angrier about making a video game purchase in my entire life. I would rather rebuy No Mans Sky than rebuy the entire game I had with DLC for another 40$ (which was cheaper than just buying all of the DLC). You would think they would at least give all of the DLC to me (you know... since it’s “complete”). Seriously this game makes EA look generous. I appreciate buying DLC if it adds flavorful content and improves on the game, I’m all for it! Really, really want to like this project. I want to say it has a bright future. The physics, the combat, the game engine itself, the platforming, are all *very* promising.  Unfortunately, in it's current state it simply (to me) not worth the backing cost at all.
Lately I've looked at my library, and I'm glad to say that out of all my titles, I regret very few purchases. Unfortunately, Overgrowth is a backing that for me is starting to look worthy of seeking a refund for. The speed of updates, the years it's been in development, and the.. state of the game/engine itself, (which grants me a low frame rate and crashes regardless of my settings, [important to note, I can run and enjoy GTAV and BF4 on this machine] even now), bring the centrally poised thumb downward.
I won't say don't support them. And I am not yet decided on whether I would seek a refund with Wolfire Games.  I believe they are honest and don't spend the funds they receive wrongly necessarily, but I also can't say I think this price is worth what is offered. If this game does come to fruition within the next 1-2 decades, I'm sure it would be a great game, with a great engine, physics, combat based on said physics, and maybe an interesting story and (possibly?) multiplayer.
As of now, you are putting your faith, and money, into a product which, (for some reason I personally cannot run very well at all), is ultimately far from finished and contains very little replay value in my view.
That said, when/if this title is *ever* finished or near finished, I imagine it would certainly be worth this price, if not more.
